articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi - a rivalry that shaped football
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi have been at the top of the game for the past 20 years, BBC Sport looks at a rivalry that has shaped football.
articles.body:
Brazil's Kaka had just won the 2007 Fifa Player of the Year award but it was an awkward on-stage moment next to him that was to go viral and provide perhaps the first glimpse of a generational rivalry.

A youthful Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo had finished second and third respectively but Brazil legend Pele mistakenly handed the latter the trophy for second place at the Zurich Opera House.

Fifa president Sepp Blatter had to intervene to ask the duo to swap the trophies, with both looking suitably unimpressed.

For the next 10 years, Messi or Ronaldo won every Ballon d'Or and Fifa award going. In fact since 2007, 20 of the 29 gongs awarded for Europe's player of the year has gone to one of them.

With approaching 2,000 career goals between them, 85 trophies for club and country and countless individual awards and records, Messi and Ronaldo will forever be remembered as two of the most decorated players in history.

It is a rivalry that has defined the last two decades of football, transcending clubs, countries and competitions to reshape how the game has been played, consumed and debated across the world.

"Two players like them, competing at that level for so many years, fighting over the Ballon d'Or and scoring that many goals... I don't think we'll see it again," Argentina World Cup winner Angel di Maria, who played with both, says in BBC Sport's new documentary Rivals: Messi v Ronaldo.

Driven by a pursuit of trophies, records and a relentless desire to be the best, the pair have pushed each other to new heights.

It is a rivalry that goes beyond the ultimate 'greatest of all time' debate they have fuelled.

"They both changed football," says Di Maria.

Ask anyone who is the greatest and agreement is hard to find.

"It has to be Ronaldo," ex-Manchester United team-mate Rio Ferdinand says.

"Messi is the best there has ever been," insists ex-Barcelona player and manager Xavi.

Ronaldo has had his say in the past, stating in 2012: "You cannot compare a Ferrari with a Porsche. It is a different engine. Some people say I am better, some people say he is. They are going to decide who is better in the moment and I think it's me."

What do the numbers tell us? If it's judged on goals or Champions League trophies, Ronaldo leads the way. If it's Ballons d'Or or total trophies, Messi shades it.

For some, Ronaldo nudged ahead when he helped Portugal lift the European Championship in 2016, but Messi has since guided Argentina to two Copa America titles and a World Cup.

"For me, Messi is the best player in history and Cristiano is the greatest goalscorer in history," says Spanish football expert Guillem Balague, who has written biographies of both players.

And Deco, who played with Ronaldo for Portugal and Messi for Barcelona, says: "They are special. They are totally different from the rest. It's not normal to be on this level all these years.

"Each year, there's a lot of players who do amazing things for a few years, but being almost 20 years is not normal."

Perhaps the beauty of the GOAT debate is that it may never be settled - and does not need to be.

"They have come to appreciate each as the co-stars of the football drama they have appeared in for the last 20 years," says Jonathan Clegg, co-author of a Ronaldo and Messi book.

The pair are seen by many as polar opposites.

The dribbler against the physical specimen. The shy genius against the arrogant ego. Pep Guardiola's Barcelona against Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid. Adidas against Nike.

But, while the narrative of their rivalry was undoubtedly built on their differences, the similarities between the two were striking - even from an early age.

Both players were raised in humble surroundings. Both left their homes at an early age to pursue their dreams - Messi to Barcelona from Argentina at 13 and Ronaldo to Lisbon from Madeira aged 12 - and both struggled with home sickness after leaving their family behind.

Wall Street Journal reporter Joshua Robinson, co-author of a Messi Ronaldo book, said: "Messi and Ronaldo are always portrayed as being so different but the things that forged them in their childhoods were incredibly similar.

"They both go to a place that says 'we will take your talent and make you even greater'. That promise feels appealing but is a huge gamble. That moment of total commitment is when they realise this isn't kid stuff any more. 'If I'm going to be the greatest of all time, this is where it begins.'"

But the biggest thing that brought the pair together was their unshakeable desire to succeed as they quickly built reputations as prodigious young talents.

"You could already see something different with Messi," said Xavi. "Not only the quality but the intensity with which he did things. There was an aggressiveness in attack that I had never seen before.

"Cristiano even gave him an extra push to be a better player."

Meanwhile in England, a teenage Ronaldo was signing for Manchester United from Sporting.

"I never met a young player so confident in knowing what he wanted," said Rene Meulensteen, who was part of the club's backroom team at the time. "The moment he came to Man United it was just a logical step of what he wanted to become - the best player in the world.

"Cristiano was a fast learner. I wanted to turn him from someone who could score a goal to a goalscorer. I made a three-minute video that just showed him scoring goals and also then the opportunities he didn't score. He embraced everything."

Fast forward to 2008 and the Champions League semi-final. Manchester United v Barcelona. Ronaldo v Messi for the first time.

"You could see already Messi was the best in La Liga and Cristiano was the best in the Premier League," said Spanish football journalist Guillem Balague. "To see those two kids on the pitch together was the sign of something to come."

Manchester United went on to win the trophy, Ronaldo lifted the Ballon d'Or and a rivalry for the ages had just begun.

Watch on BBC iPlayer from 06:00 BST on Friday, 5 June

"There is no doubt being in the same league changed everything," says Txiki Begiristain, director of football at Barcelona between 2003 and 2010.

Ronaldo's world record £80m move to Real Madrid in 2009 thrust the pair right into the centre of one of football's most intense club rivalries - Barcelona v Real Madrid.

And by the time Ronaldo left for Juventus in 2018, the pair had won five Ballons d'Or apiece. In the nine seasons the pair were together in Spain, Ronaldo had scored 450 goals in 438 games for Real. Messi, 471 in 476 games for Barca.

But it had become far more than just numbers. By now, it was personal - and the growth of social media meant the world was watching.

"For Cristiano it was Lionel Messi and for Lionel Messi it was Cristiano. 'I need to beat this guy'," said Begiristain.

"The Mourinho - Guardiola rivalry was like a mirror for the Ronaldo - Messi rivalry. And, as players, they knew that game-winning goals were their route to one-upmanship," added Spanish football writer Sid Lowe.

"We could watch it all on our phones. And in turn, the global exposure for the Messi - Ronaldo rivalry was now sky high, absolutely off the charts. Everything they did was must-see.

"It was on everyone's lips in the press box, newspapers and social media comments, Cristiano and Leo were hell bent on outdoing each other on the pitch. Their personal battle for supremacy was symbolised by the ongoing trophy battle between the clubs."

And what a battle it was. Messi and Barcelona undoubtedly won the La Liga honours, but the Champions League was dominated by Real Madrid and Ronaldo.

In 2012, Ronaldo inspired Real to their first La Liga title in four years but it was Messi who picked up his fourth straight Ballon d'Or award - much to his rival's disgust. He went to win four of the next five.

"There is a genuine animosity that begins to grow," says Robinson. "They didn't acknowledge each other that much, they hated comparisons.

"They could not tolerate if they were the greatest of all time, there could be another in their era, in their football league."

Deco adds: "I don't think there is something similar to what happened with Messi and Ronaldo at this moment because at the same time the two clubs, Barcelona and Madrid, were at the same level and fighting for the big trophies."

When Messi scored a 92nd-minute winner for Barcelona at Real Madrid in 2017, he removed his jersey and held it up the crowd.

"In the popular narrative, Cristiano had been the diva and Messi had been the humble servant of Barcelona, but this was the moment of Messi reasserting himself on the rivalry, saying maybe for the first time in his career 'look at me'," says Robinson.

Just a few months later, Ronaldo mimicked the celebration when he scored in the Spanish Super Cup at Barcelona.

Balague added: "If you needed proof of how much it meant to beat each other, those are the pictures."

The Messi v Ronaldo rivalry in Spain may have ended when the latter joined Juventus in 2018 - but the global, ongoing debate wasn't disappearing.

Ronaldo went on to return to Manchester United before moving to current club Al-Nassr in Saudi Arabia, while Messi moved to Paris St-Germain, before signing for Inter Miami in America's Major League Soccer - where he remains now.

Having seen their impact in Spain, for the first time the players' moves were as commercially motivated as they were for football reasons.

"Brand Beckham opened the door for what was possible and these two have kicked the door off its hinges," said Rob Pilgrim, head of sport at Meta for Europe, Middle East and Africa.

Italian football expert Mina Rzouki, added: "You are not buying sporting excellence, you are buying a whole one-man economy."

The numbers are astronomical and the rivalry continued.

In 2018, Ronaldo joins Juventus and sells 520,000 shirts in the first 24 hours. In 2021, Messi moves to Paris and shifts 150,000 shirts in just seven minutes.

Manchester United welcome Ronaldo back in 2021, and United's total sales of his shirt (£187m) are almost double those of Messi's at PSG.

On Instagram, Ronaldo has close to 700m followers, Messi has 500m. The most-liked picture in the history of that platform is the Argentine lifting the World Cup trophy, amassing more than 75m likes.

Financially, Ronaldo comes out on top - according to official channels anyway. The Portuguese has topped the Forbes Money List as the world's highest paid athlete for a fourth consecutive time, with $300m (£223m) in total earnings. Messi is third on the list with $140m (£104m).

The rivalry between the pair is only accentuated by the fact they are on either side of the sportswear rivalry. Messi with Adidas and Ronaldo with Nike.

"They have become enormous global brands and what is amazing about them is they have to say almost nothing to become the world's biggest pitch man," said Robinson.

Brands the world over threw unparalleled amounts of money to get the superstars on board.

And who could forget the iconic image before the 2022 World Cup in Qatar, with both footballers playing chess against each other on a Louis Vuitton suitcase, to launch the designer's latest campaign.

"It is known as the picture that broke the internet. It was a commercial masterstroke," said Melanie Ropp, from social media marketing company the Goat Agency. "The timing of it before the World Cup made it globally iconic."

Robinson said: "Messi has nothing left to conquer. He has that one thing Ronaldo does not, a World Cup."

And, after following the Argentine in announcing his retirement from international football, it appears the global prize will continue to elude Ronaldo.

"Now the question is did Messi win this entire era of football?" adds Robinson.

articles.title: Moto do Batman vai a leilão | G1
articles.standfirst: Batpod tem 3,80 metros de comprimento, conjunto de rodas e pneus de 31 polegadas e foi pilotado nos filmes da trilogia do diretor Christopher Nolan.
articles.summary: Batpod tem 3,80 metros de comprimento, conjunto de rodas e pneus de 31 polegadas e foi pilotado nos filmes da trilogia do diretor Christopher Nolan.
articles.body:
Batpod usado no filme “Batman: O Cavaleiro das Trevas” de 2008 vai a leilão. — Foto: Divulgação / Propstore

A moto que Batman usou para perseguir o Coringa em “ Batman: O Cavaleiro das Trevas ” (2008) vai a leilão em Londres. Os lances podem ser feitos pela internet até o dia 4 de dezembro.

A Propstore, responsável pelo pregão, estima que a Batpod seja arrematada por um valor que pode chegar a 900 mil libras ( R$ 6,6 milhões em conversão direta e sem impostos). Riscos e outras marcas no lado direito da moto permitiram identificar o exemplar nas imagens da perseguição.

No filme, Batman, interpretado por Christian Bale, escapa do batmóvel destruído e segue sobre duas rodas atrás do Coringa, papel de Heath Ledger.

A moto voltou às telas em “ Batman: O Cavaleiro das Trevas Ressurge ” (2012). Dessa vez, tanto o herói quanto Selina Kyle, interpretada por Anne Hathaway, pilotam a Batpod no confronto com Bane e a Liga das Sombras.

Quem arrematar a Batpod só poderá movê-la empurrando . A moto está sem bateria, tanque de combustível e comandos do acelerador. Todos os fluidos foram drenados, e o lote inclui um suporte de metal para exposição.

O diretor Christopher Nolan e o designer de produção Nathan Crowley imaginaram a Batpod como uma opção mais ágil que o Tumbler, batmóvel que era baseado num tanque futurista.

Crowley concluiu o desenho, e o supervisor de efeitos especiais, Chris Corbould, construiu seis unidades para o filme de 2008 .

Os pneus de competição Hoosier de 31 polegadas eram tão largos que dificultaram o trabalho de quem precisou fazer a moto rodar.

Nas filmagens, o dublê Jean-Pierre Goy pilotava deitado de bruços e usava os braços e os ombros para mudar de direção. Os comandos dos freios ficavam na manopla esquerda e no pedal direito.

Com 3,80 metros de comprimento, 1,20 metro de largura e 1,07 metro de altura, a Batpod tem motor Honda 750 e escapamento integrado ao chassi. Painéis de fibra de vidro pintados de cinza metálico cobrem o motor e o guidão.

Na dianteira, os canos dos dois canhões cenográficos são de plástico, resina e fibra de vidro. Acima da manopla direita fica uma mira que se ilumina.

A moto fez parte do acervo da Warner Bros . e foi usada em eventos de divulgação dos dois filmes. Além dos riscos que a identificam em cena, há desgaste nos painéis, pontos de corrosão no chassi e um dano no suporte do canhão esquerdo, ocorrido durante as filmagens.

Esta será a segunda passagem da Batpod por um leilão da Propstore . A Warner Bros. vendeu a moto em 27 de setembro de 2016. O exemplar volta à venda com certificado de autenticidade do estúdio.

articles.title: Kylian Mbappe creates Champions League history, joins Lionel Messi in elite list
articles.summary: Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappe added another milestone to his impressive UEFA Champions League career on Wednesday, becoming the second-fastest player
articles.body: Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappe added another milestone to his impressive UEFA Champions League career on Wednesday, becoming the second-fastest player to register 100 goal contributions in the competition's history.The French superstar reached the landmark during Real Madrid's clash against AEK Athens, finding the net in the 78th minute to take his combined tally of goals and assists to 100. Mbappe has now recorded 74 goals and 26 assists in 102 Champions League appearances.Only Lionel Messi reached the milestone quicker, taking 101 matches to register 100 goal contributions. The Argentina great achieved the feat while representing Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain (PSG) before moving to Major League Soccer (MLS), where he currently plays for Inter Miami.Cristiano Ronaldo remains at the top of the all-time Champions League goal contributions chart with 182, comprising 140 goals and 42 assists.Mbappe milestone as Real Madrid stage comeback against AEK AthensThe record-breaking moment came during an eventful encounter in Athens, where Real Madrid had to fight back after falling behind twice before eventually securing a 3-2 victory.AEK Athens made an early breakthrough through Aboubakary Koita, who opened the scoring in the 12th minute following an assist from Luka Jovic.Real Madrid thought they had found an equaliser when Vinicius Jr's cross ended up in the net following a touch from Jude Bellingham. However, the goal was ruled out because the English midfielder was adjudged to be offside.Bellingham made up for the disallowed effort just three minutes later, producing an excellent backheel finish in the 32nd minute to bring Madrid back into the contest, as reported by Goal.com.Mbappe also had an opportunity to create danger when he picked out an unmarked Marc Cucurella, but the latter failed to make the most of the chance with his weaker foot.The hosts regained the advantage in the 75th minute, with Koita turning provider this time by setting up Stavro Pilo, who put AEK Athens on the verge of a memorable victory.However, Madrid responded almost immediately. Denzel Dumfries delivered a cross that Mbappe converted in the 78th minute, restoring parity while simultaneously bringing up his 100th Champions League goal contribution.With the match heading towards its conclusion, Federico Valverde stepped up with a stunning strike, finding the top corner to complete Madrid's comeback and seal a dramatic 3-2 win.The victory ensured that Mbappe's personal milestone was accompanied by another important result for Real Madrid in Europe.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Cole Palmer: A must pick or unreliable? Thomas Tuchel's dilemma over Chelsea star
articles.summary: Will Thomas Tuchel pick Cole Palmer for his next England squad as the competition to be England's number 10 continues.
articles.body:
Has Cole Palmer done enough to earn an England call-up for their November Nations League games against Croatia and Spain?

The 24-year-old Chelsea forward is regarded as one of the stars at Stamford Bridge, but his status with the Three Lions has been the subject of major debate, particularly since Thomas Tuchel's appointment as manager at the beginning of 2025.

Palmer's withdrawal from the most recent extended three-week camp came after his omission from their World Cup squad, prompting Tuchel to say he "misses too many opportunities to play for England" .

Yet there is an argument Palmer has done enough to earn an England recall with his start to this campaign - despite Tuchel's obvious reservations.

Having scored five goals and provided three assists in all competitions, only his Chelsea team-mate Morgan Rogers has had more goal involvements during the opening months of the campaign - when looking at players he is in competition with for England.

It must be noted, though, that penalties do inflate Palmer's total more than that of some of those rivals for a Three Lions spot.

When spot-kicks are excluded, he has been outscored by all of the alternatives for England's number 10 role since the beginning of last season. He has also been outscored in open play by Rogers and Real Madrid's Jude Bellingham this season.

In addition, Manchester City 's Phil Foden, who - along with Palmer - was also left out of the World Cup squad, has the same number of goal involvements (eight) this season, although half of those came against AEK Athens in the Champions League.

Nottingham Forest 's Morgan Gibbs-White has also created just as many chances (2.6 per game), although they are not being converted by his team-mates.

While Gibbs-White has underperformed his expected goals this season, he has outscored Palmer since the beginning of the 2025-26 campaign and also replaced him in Tuchel's most recent squad.

Palmer compared favourably with Arsenal 's Eberechi Eze, who, along with Bellingham and Rogers, was selected ahead of the Chelsea attacker for the World Cup , where England took the bronze medal after losing to Argentina in the semi-finals.

Yet Palmer has struggled to make an impact under Tuchel, making just three appearances, including two starts, without scoring or providing an assist.

Bellingham, meanwhile, was named the national team's player of the year for 2026 after scoring seven goals and providing one assist during an outstanding World Cup campaign over the summer.

In terms of Palmer's direct rivals, Bellingham leads the way with eight goals and six assists during Tuchel's nearly two years in charge, while Rogers is second with three goals and three assists.

In third is Eze, who has scored three times and had one assist under Tuchel's tenure.

But Palmer, Foden and Gibbs-White will all be eyeing Eze's spot when the squad is announced on Friday (11:00 GMT).

Palmer missed Tuchel's first camp with a hamstring injury in March 2025, but went on to play 90 minutes in Chelsea 's first Premier League match after that international break.

He then featured in the June fixtures, playing in a 1-0 win away to Andorra before being an unused substitute in a friendly defeat by Senegal.

During the September, October and November international breaks that followed, Palmer was managing a recurring groin problem, which severely limited his club appearances during the early part of last season.

He last featured for England in March, coming on as a substitute in the 56th minute of a 1-1 draw with Uruguay before starting against Japan, where he lasted only 59 minutes in a 1-0 home defeat.

Palmer then withdrew from the most recent international break, with Gibbs-White replacing him, after saying he had played for Chelsea with "discomfort and pain" before the call-up.

Boss Xabi Alonso has since said the attacker was "struggling" in the 3-0 loss by Brentford before the international break.

Palmer then went on an overseas holiday during a nine-day break for Chelsea 's non-international players.

He took a rehabilitation coach with him and underwent an injury-specific training plan to recover.

Returning to training with Chelsea after the period of rest, Palmer signed a new contract until 2034 at Stamford Bridge .

He then played 88 minutes and provided an assist in a 5-1 victory over Bournemouth .

He has since started all of Chelsea 's subsequent matches, apart from their EFL Cup penalty shootout defeat by Liverpool last week when he was ruled out by suspension. This followed his dismissal after receiving two yellow cards in the space of nine minutes during the home league defeat by Tottenham just over a week earlier.

Saturday's 2-0 win over Manchester United was his last appearance before Tuchel picks his squad on Friday, with his penalty taking his tally to five goals and three assists in 11 matches.

Chelsea manager Alonso, said of Palmer's absences from England duty: "He's committed but he needs to be fully fit to play and when he's fully fit he will enjoy his minutes.

"We need him in that moment, [both] the club and the national team."

Tuchel has, however, expressed frustration over the player and said he "misses too many opportunities" to play for England.

If Palmer is not selected, his lack of availability will likely be a major factor in the decision.

articles.title: Champions League: Liverpool suffer 3-2 loss at Fenerbahce, Como thump Lens
articles.summary: Como equal Champions League record with stunning 9-1 win at Lens as Haaland rescues Manchester City at Leipzig.
articles.body:
Fenerbahce’s interim ‌‌head coach Dirk Kuyt has praised his side’s intensity and ⁠⁠fighting spirit ⁠⁠after they twice came from behind to beat his former club Liverpool 3-2 at home in the ⁠⁠Champions League.

Just two matches into the job, the Dutchman delivered Fenerbahce’s first victory of ‌‌their Champions League campaign, thanks to Vedat Muriqi’s 79th-minute winner on Wednesday.

Kuyt, who played more than 200 games for Liverpool between 2006 and 2012, was last ⁠⁠week named interim coach of Fenerbahce while they search for a permanent manager following the resignation of Ismail Kartal.

“I’m very happy with all the players and all the people who were involved in making a miracle tonight because I think not many people expected us to win [playing] Liverpool,” Kuyt said after the match.

Liverpool arrived in Istanbul with three wins from three but Muriqi’s winner ended that run.

Trey Nyoni opened the scoring in the 25th minute, meeting a defensive header with a low volley that deflected off Kojo Peprah Oppong and wrong-footed Fenerbahce keeper Ederson.

Mason Greenwood levelled four minutes later with a free kick that struck Jeremy Jacquet in the defensive wall and skidded past Alisson.

Substitutes Cody Gakpo and Alexander Isak combined to restore Liverpool’s lead in the 69th minute. Gakpo exchanged passes with Kostas Tsimikas before reaching the byline and delivering a cross for Isak to power a close-range header past Ederson.

The advantage lasted four minutes. Following a short corner, N’Golo Kante crossed and Gakpo’s glancing header diverted the ball away from Alisson, leaving Archie Brown to tap into an unguarded net at the far post.

Brown then supplied the winner, looping the ball into the box after a long throw was headed back to him. Surrounded by three Liverpool defenders, Muriqi somehow headed past Alisson, wrapping up a poor night for Liverpool’s defence.

Andoni Iraola’s side dropped to eighth with nine points, while Fenerbahce climbed to 19th on five.

Meanwhile, Como stormed into the Champions League record books with a stunning 9-1 demolition ⁠⁠of Lens, equalling the biggest victory in the competition’s history.

The Italian side matched the eight-goal winning margins achieved by Liverpool and Real Madrid in 8-0 ⁠⁠home victories over Besiktas and Malmo respectively.

Como also became the first team since 1971 to score nine goals away from home in the European Cup and only the second ⁠⁠after Bayern Munich to score nine in a Champions League match.

Their third victory in four matches lifted them to fourth in the standings on nine points and continued a remarkable debut campaign in which they have scored 19 goals.

“It’s an incredible night,” Como captain Lucas ‌‌Da Cunha said.

“We started with a lot of desire, we wanted to take the three points, like we always do, and this evening we were able to do that.

“It’s a crazy night and a crazy result, but we can’t get ahead of ourselves.”

Real Madrid conjure comeback win at AEK Athens

It took a Federico Valverde stoppage-time goal to give Real Madrid a dramatic 3-2 victory at AEK Athens.

Real twice came from behind to maintain their perfect start and sit second on 12 points from four matches, behind Paris Saint-Germain on goal difference.

AEK threatened from the outset and their early pressure was rewarded in the 12th minute when Aboubakary Koita cut inside and fired into the top corner from just inside the box.

Thibaut Courtois denied Luka Jovic before Jude Bellingham, who had an effort ruled out for offside in the 27th minute, equalised five minutes later with a deft backheel from Marc Cucurella’s low cross.

Koita’s driving run and pass set up Stavros Pilios to restore AEK’s lead in the 75th minute, his low shot going through Courtois’ legs.

Kylian Mbappe tapped in Denzel Dumfries’ cross three minutes later before Valverde delivered the winner, leaving AEK 29th on three points.

Man City led through Castello Lukeba’s 37th-minute own goal as he tried to clear Nico O’Reilly’s cross, but Ridle Baku equalised four minutes after half-time.

Enzo Fernandez restored City’s advantage in the 58th minute before Antonio Nusa levelled three minutes later. Elliot Anderson’s run and low cross then found Haaland, who slid in to finish at the far post.

City are seventh on nine points, six points clear of Leipzig, who are in the elimination places.

First-half goals from Noni Madueke and Viktor Gyokeres put Arsenal in control in Prague. Wiktor Nowak punished Arsenal’s failure to clear a cross in the final minute, but Slavia remained 34th on one point.

articles.title: Iraola confiesa que el "ruido ensordecedor" del infierno turco afectó a su Liverpool en un gol
articles.summary: "Son goles regalados. Son goles embarullados"
articles.body: Andoni Iraola analiza la derrota del Liverpool por 3-2 ante el Fenerbahçe en Champions League, y señala al ruido del Chobani Stadium como responsable del segundo gol del equipo turco que marcó Archie Brown. "Son goles regalados. Son goles embarullados", reconoció el técnico español, que tras encadenar cinco victorias consecutivas, ha sufrido dos derrotas en apenas cuatro días. Iraola, que compartió su frustración por encajar tres goles a balón parado, comentó que "la falta es desde una distancia considerable, pasando a través de la barrera. El último gol llegó tras un saque de banda largo; en el segundo, Cody (Gakpo) tocó el balón justo delante de Alisson". "En el estadio era casi imposible comunicarse debido al ruido ensordecedor; me resultó difícil dar instrucciones, y la comunicación entre Cody y Ali también fue complicada", apuntó culpando al ensordecedor ambiente que había en el Chobani Stadium. Sobre los fallos a balón de parado de su equipo reconoció que "es un aspecto que veníamos trabajando muy bien en la Premier; lo estábamos haciendo bastante bien hasta el día de hoy. Sabíamos que era uno de los puntos fuertes del Fenerbahçe. Nos marcaron en un tiro libre, en un saque de esquina e incluso en ese saque de banda largo al final". "Siento frustración, porque es un campo muy difícil en el que jugar. Durante la mayor parte del encuentro, creímos que podíamos ganar. Pero, obviamente, no ha sido así", reconoció. Kostas Tsimikas, defensa del Liverpool, reconoció que la zaga inglesa no estuvo a su mejor nivel ante el Fenerbahçe que dirigió de forma interina Dirk Kuyt (ídolo de la afición 'red'): "No defendimos bien después del gol que encajamos. Apenas tres o cuatro minutos más tarde, recibimos otro gol de forma inmediata. Creo que debemos marcar mejor si queremos ganar partidos". Dirk Kuyt, que entrenó al Fenerbahçe de forma interina hasta la llegada de Emre Belozoglu (ex del Atlético), confesó que "Esta noche hemos obrado un milagro; pocos esperaban que ganáramos. Fue una noche muy especial para todos los que aman al Fenerbahçe. Quiero felicitar enormemente a los jugadores y al cuerpo técnico, que no dejan de impulsarlos". "Nos dijimos que debíamos mantenernos unidos y permanecer juntos. Es algo que aprendí en el Liverpool, nuestro rival de esta noche. Hemos logrado un milagro; pocos esperaban que ganáramos", apuntó.

articles.title: La Policía investiga como asesinato la muerte del futbolista inglés Ezekiel Williams
articles.standfirst: Ezekiel Williams, futbolista de 26 años del Hendon FC, murió en el hospital tras ser herido en un incidente en la calle
articles.summary: Ezekiel Williams, futbolista de 26 años del Hendon FC, murió en el hospital tras ser herido en un incidente en la calle
articles.body: Ezekiel Williams, futbolista inglés de 26 años que militaba en el Hendon FC, murió tras sufrir heridas graves en un incidente en Milton Keynes (Gran Bretaña). La policía de Thames Valley informó que los agentes recibieron un aviso del servicio de ambulancias South Central, y que Williams falleció en el hospital el lunes a consecuencia de las heridas sufridas. La Policía investiga la muerte de Ezekiel Williams como un homicidio, y dos hombres han sido detenidos como sospechosos de asesinato. Un tercer hombre ha sido detenido bajo la sospecha de haber colaborado. Los tres están en prisión preventiva. "Estamos llevando a cabo una investigación exhaustiva y detallada para determinar qué ocurrió exactamente. Somos conscientes de que este suceso generará preocupación en la comunidad local", declaró el inspector jefe de policía Rob Underhill. Ezekiel Williams, que fue recordado como "una persona humilde, sencilla y generosa, dotada de un ingenio agudísimo", fichó por el Hendon FC en septiembre. "Hace apenas 10 días, marcó su primer gol con el club contra el Jersey Bulls", apuntaron desde el Hendon FC, equipo que milita en la Isthmian League South Central Division (octava categoría del fútbol inglés). A lo largo de su trayectoria futbolística Ezekiel Williams jugó en el Kettering Town FC, FC Romania, Northwood y Harrow Borough.

articles.title: Liverpool: Trey Nyoni and Rio Ngumoha starring shows Reds haven't spent money well enough, says Jamie Carragher
articles.summary: Liverpool lost 3-2 to Fenerbahce on Wednesday night; speaking on CBS Sports, Carragher said: "It [the defeat] reinforces to supporters the squad Liverpool have got is very expensive, but not as good as it should be and not as balanced as it should be"
articles.body:
The Reds were 2-1 up with 20 minutes to play in Istanbul but went on to lose 3-2 in a game where teenagers Trey Nyoni and Rio Ngumoha again starred.

Nyoni scored the opener and Alexander Isak hit the second, but Bradley Barcola extended his run of scoring in just one of his 13 appearances for the club so far.

"It [defeat to Fenerbahce] reinforces to supporters that the squad Liverpool have got is very expensive, but not as good as it should be and not as balanced as it should be," said Carragher, speaking on CBS Sports .

"When you think of some of those players that have come in, what's a little worry for not so much the manager, but the people who run the club... Trey Nyoni and Rio Ngumoha were the best players for Liverpool, and they were a week or so ago against Chelsea.

"But they also play in the position of players where Liverpool have spent big money.

"Bradley Barcola has come in for £120m. He played up front tonight, didn't play well, but the younger players are playing better than him.

"And in Nyoni in midfield; Liverpool haven't spent expensively on a player as such, but they've given big contracts this summer to Ryan Gravenberch - who was left out at the weekend for Nyoni - and Szoboszlai who played tonight and didn't play particularly well.

"You can imagine the type of figures they would be on and when a young player in midfield is playing ahead of them that causes a problem about where you've spent your money - and you basically haven't spent your money well enough."

Liverpool's spending over the last three seasons

2025/26 : Alexander Isak (£125m), Florian Wirtz (£116m), Hugo Ekitike (£79m), Milos Kerkez (£40m), Jeremie Frimpong (£29.5m), Giorgi Mamardashvili (£29m), Giovanni Leoni (£26m), Armin Pesci (£1.5m), Freddie Woodman (Free)

2026/27 : Bradley Barcola (£123m), Jeremy Jacquet (£60m), Victor Munoz (£34.5m), Ifeanyi Ndukwe (Undisclosed)

Youthful attack let down by experienced defence

Analysis from Sky Sports' Callum Bishop:

The average age of Liverpool's starting front three was less than 22. The average age of their defence was just shy of 30.

On a European night and in a hostile environment, you'd expect it would be the experienced heads who stepped up. But the opposite was the case in Istanbul.

Nineteen-year-old Trey Nyoni stole the show on the night where he became the club's second-youngest Champions League goalscorer. Meanwhile, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz had their moments threatening the Fenerbahce backline.

Yet, at the back, Liverpool looked stuck in the mud. The state of the wall for Fenerbahce's first was well below par and Jacquet paid the price with the deflection. The marking and miscommunication that led to the second was also shocking to see.

But the third was the biggest failure. With the ball high in the sky, Muriqi drifted away from Virgil van Dijk, beat three static red shirts and headed past Alisson.

If Iraola was looking for a response after the defeat at Anfield, he would have been banking on that back five to be the leading lights within one. Instead, they are the reason he has suffered back-to-back defeats for the first time since taking the Anfield hot seat.

articles.title: Todos son Owono: "No va a estar solo"
articles.standfirst: El Andorra, con Piqué al frente, se vuelca con el portero guineano que está en shock y aún no ha podido asimilar la tragedia
articles.summary: El Andorra, con Piqué al frente, se vuelca con el portero guineano que está en shock y aún no ha podido asimilar la tragedia
articles.body: "Sentirse culpable no es tener la culpa", la frase de José Ortiz, psicólogo deportivo, en TD resuena en las oficinas del Andorra. "No va a estar solo", esa se repite sin cesar hables con quién hables. Owono está en buenas manos. Destrozado por dentro, refugiado en casa y rodeado de su gente más cercana. Así pasa las horas el portero del Andorra, protagonista accidental de uno de los sucesos más luctuosos de la historia del fútbol español. Un drama. Desde que el equipo regresó a la capital del Principado, Owono no ha pisado la calle. Su madre es la que está tirando del carro ayudada de un buen número de amigos del fútbol que se han plantado en Andorra a la carrera. Ex compañeros con los que empezó a jugar en Vitoria y en San Sebastián que han hecho las maletas y han conducido hasta su casa para estar a su lado en estos momentos. También sus agentes, los que han conducido su carrera desde hace mucho tiempo, están en Andorra ayudando en todo lo que se necesita. La gente del club, con un Piqué que se ha volcado con el chico y está en todo momento al pie del cañón, se ha multiplicado para estar cerca. Sus compañeros, los entrenadores, los empleados... todos están pendientes de que el guineano se sostenga con las pocas fuerzas que le quedan. Ha llorado y sigue llorando a cada instante, es imposible superar una situación así sin tiempo, pero poco a poco el ambiente irrespirable (muchas veces generado por cuatro energúmenos) va dejando paso al sentido común. "Nunca le haría daño a nadie", comentaba uno de los capitanes del equipo. La tragedia le ha golpeado, ver morir a su compañero de trabajo tras el accidente ha sido demasiado duro. Sus propios compañeros están necesitando ayuda de profesionales para salir adelante. Cada vez que les viene a la cabeza la imagen del desastre nadie puede aguantar sereno. Desde el club se ha pedido el máximo respeto... y en Andorra, el Principado se ha volcado con el duelo por la muerte de Jesús y en ayudar a salir del pozo a Owono. La Federación de fútbol del país vecino ha decretado un minuto de silencio en todos los partidos de este fin de semana. El respeto es total y el dolor inmenso. Este miércoles, el entrenador del equipo preparó una sesión voluntaria en el campo Comunal Joan Samarra. "Para verse y hacer piña y no estar todo el día en casa", aseguraban desde la entidad. Owono no asistió, pero casi todos sus compañeros, que guardaron un doloroso minuto de silencio sí lo hicieron. Al respeto se unieron los empleados y algunos atletas que entrenaban en las pistas anexas. Si no pasa nada extraño este jueves el equipo va a volver a trabajar, no hay partido a la vista, porque el del fin de semana se ha suspendido, pero resulta complicado pensar que ese grupo humano pueda volver a competir en breve. "La pelota cura", pero hay veces que necesita tiempo y en este caso va a ser muy necesario. La figura de Gerard Piqué está siendo clave en estos momentos. El máximo accionista del club está encima de todo, a cada instante. Este jueves encabezará la comitiva en señal de duelo que se desplazará a Navahermosa, el pueblo de los padres de Jesús de Miguel, junto a Ferran Villaseca (presidente del Andorra) y a Jaume Nogues (director general y deportivo). Quieren estar presentas, dar el pésame, intentar ayudar en lo que sea necesario y unirse al dolor de una familia que llora una pérdida irreparable. Los gestos de dolor han recorrido España y también los gestos de ayuda. La AFE (Asociación de Futbolistas Españoles) está trabajando a destajo. Desde la entidad se transmite que no van a dejar solo a Owono y que nadie se ha olvidado de él. Van a ayudar a todos los jugadores. Por supuesto a la plantilla del Tenerife que está en shock emocional y también al portero y a sus compañeros del Andorra.

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo announces international retirement
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo has announced his intention to retire from international football, bringing an end to one of the most remarkable careers in the history
articles.body: Cristiano Ronaldo has announced his intention to retire from international football, bringing an end to one of the most remarkable careers in the history of the game. The Portugal captain confirmed his decision through a social media post on Thursday, revealing that he would 'hand back the number 7 shirt' following the November international break.The 41-year-old leaves behind an extraordinary legacy in Portuguese football, having established himself as the most prolific goalscorer and the most-capped player in men's international football.Ronaldo has represented Portugal in 234 matches, scoring an incredible 146 goals since making his international debut against Kazakhstan on August 20, 2003. His first international goal came against Greece during UEFA Euro 2004, a tournament that marked the beginning of his journey towards becoming one of football's greatest-ever players.Cristiano Ronaldo shared a heartfelt message with his fans in his retirement video. "To the Portuguese people, the day has come for me to hand back the No. 7 shirt of our national team,” the 41-year-old Ronaldo said in a long video message on social media."I never felt it belonged to me alone but for 23 years I had the privilege and the responsibility of wearing it, defending it and carrying it with me into stadiums all around the world.”Cristiano Ronaldo's international career: Goals, appearances and recordsRonaldo's numbers for Portugal underline his extraordinary consistency and longevity at the international level. With 146 goals in 234 appearances, he remains comfortably ahead of every other player on the men's international goalscoring charts.He has also registered 10 international hat-tricks, alongside two occasions when he scored four goals in a single match.Of his 146 international goals, 124 have come in competitive fixtures, including FIFA World Cup matches, European Championships, UEFA Nations League games and qualifiers. The remaining 22 goals have been scored in international friendlies.His international career began in August 2003, and he went on to become Portugal's all-time leading goalscorer and appearance-maker.Six World Cups, European Championship glory and Nations League titlesAt the FIFA World Cup, he became the first player to score in six different editions of the tournament, achieving the milestone across the 2006, 2010, 2014, 2018, 2022 and 2026 editions. He has scored 11 goals in World Cup history.At the European Championship, Ronaldo holds the all-time goalscoring record with 14 goals across six tournaments. His most memorable international achievement came in 2016, when he captained Portugal to their first-ever European Championship title. He also played a significant role in Portugal's UEFA Nations League triumphs in 2019 and 2025.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo retires from international football after glittering Portugal career that spanned 23 years
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo has retired from international duty with Portugal; the 41-year-old earned 234 caps, scoring 146 goals; he won Euro 2016 and two Nations League titles for his country; it comes after a falling out with head coach Jorge Jesus in the last international break
articles.body:
The 41-year-old Portugal legend has brought an end to his glittering 23-year career for his country after a record-breaking 146 goals in 234 caps.

Ronaldo took to social media to confirm the decision on Thursday morning, with the caption "Portugal will always be in me."

You can read the statement in full at the bottom of this article.

He won Euro 2016 with his country, as well as two Nations League titles in 2019 and 2025. Portugal exited the most recent World Cup in the round of 16, beaten by eventual champions Spain.

Having made his international debut in 2003, Ronaldo played in 12 major tournaments: six World Cups and six European Championships.

The Al Nassr forward said after the tournament would be his last , later adding he would not make any rash decisions.

However, his retirement comes after a fall-out with head coach Jorge Jesus in the previous international break.

He said: "Today I finish my walk on the pitch with the national team. I leave with my head held high, with pride in the path I took, and with the awareness that I gave everything I had for Portugal.

"The goals pass, the cups are in museums, the records end up being beaten. But there is something that time can never erase, the place we occupy in people's hearts.

"I spent my life working to be the best player in the world. Today I realise that the greatest victory was to have deserved to represent the best country in the world."

Ronaldo thanked his team-mates, coaches, family and supporters around the world, adding: "Thank you for these 23 years. Thank you for having believed in me. Portugal will always be in me. Forever."

He was set to be named in the Portugal squad by head coach Jesus on Friday, but Ronaldo did not want to play under the head coach after their falling out. He has not spoken to Jesus since September 30.

Portugal are top of Nations League Group A4 with a 100 per cent record. They are playing Denmark at home a week on Saturday and Wales in Cardiff on November 17.

Ronaldo publicly admitted in the last international break that he considered ending his Portugal career following the World Cup.

A statement on Instagram revealed that Ronaldo had written his retirement statement only to be talked out of it by the president of the Portuguese Football Federation Pedro Proenca on the plane back from North America.

Portuguese federation: Ronaldo symbol of our spirit

The Portuguesa Football Federation posted a tribute to their now-former captain, crediting his extraordinary career and dedcation to his country.

They added that a fitting tribute will be paid to Ronaldo in the future, with his final game for Portugal proving to be a 1-0 win against Wales.

A statement read: "It is with a feeling of profound gratitude and immense admiration that the Portuguese Football Federation publicly praises and thanks Cristiano Ronaldo for his absolutely extraordinary career serving our country.

"More than just an outstanding athlete, our captain was an inspiring leader, an example of dedication, and the ultimate symbol of the spirit of our national team.

"Throughout a legendary international career, marked by 234 caps and 146 goals scored, the captain carried the country on his shoulders, broke records, and led the team to moments that will forever be etched in the history of national football.

"Every drop of sweat, every decisive goal, and every captain's armband worn with pride on the field reflected his unconditional love for our jersey.

"Thank you for everything, CAPTAIN! This will always be your home! Let's go for goal 1,000!"

Jesus took over from Roberto Martinez after the World Cup. His first games were Nations League fixtures in the September-October international break. His started Ronaldo in the first - a 1-0 win against Wales.

However, the then-Portugal captain was benched during a 2-1 win against Norway and did not come on.

Ronaldo left the national team camp on the eve of facing Denmark on October 1, sparking rumours that he was about to announce his international retirement.

Jesus denied there was a rift between the two despite reports - but a statement posted by Ronaldo on Instagram said the new manager had 'broken his promises'.

Ronaldo claimed that Jesus told him he would play 30 minutes against Norway on the day of the game only to go back on his word.

"Everyone knows the rest. I warmed up from half-time onwards, watched the minutes tick by and wasn't called on," Ronaldo said. "The coach had broken his word to me."

Ronaldo and Jesus, who used to work together at Al Nassr, subsequently held a meeting after the Norway game , which was also attended by the sporting director of the Saudi Pro League club, Simao Coutinho.

According to Ronaldo's statement, Jesus agreed to clarify the situation and say that his captain never demanded minutes and that it was a mistake to let him warm up without bringing him on.

Ronaldo says an eight-point document was drawn up to summarise what had been discussed in a subsequent meeting between Jesus, Al Nassr sporting director Coutinho and Tiago Craveiro, the player's strategic adviser.

However, Ronaldo felt the Portugal head coach's subsequent press conference bore no reflection to the conversation they had shared, which he claims ended in Jesus asking him for a hug.

He added: "It was the second time he had broken his word to me. I decided to leave the training camp without waiting for any further broken promises."

Jesus denied that any such agreement had been made with the player in a later press conference.

Despite this, Ronaldo admitted he never should have left the Portugal camp "despite the absolute breach of trust" from Jesus.

Ronaldo apologised to his team-mates and the Portuguese people over his departure from the squad and said he will accept whatever punishment is handed down to him by the Portuguese Football Federation.

That turned out to be a 30-day ban and a £215 fine .

"To the Portuguese people, the day has come for me to hand back the number seven shirt to the national team. I never felt it belonged to me alone. But, for 23 years, I had the privilege and the responsibility of wearing it, defending it and carrying it with me into stadiums all over the world.

"Today, the time has come to carry it into the future. It was not an easy decision, because some decisions are not made with the mind alone. They are also made with the heart. A journey that began in August 2003 and changed my life forever has come to an end.

"When I look back at everything I experienced with the national team, I don't just see matches, goals, records or trophies. I see people. I see Portuguese people living abroad who, for ninety minutes, felt a little closer to home. I see millions of Portuguese people I have never met, but who became part of my life. Because, at the end of the day, football is so much bigger than a game. Football is about people.

"Throughout my career with the national team, I always pushed myself beyond my limits. I wanted to win. I wanted to be better. I wanted to make history. I always demanded the most of myself. I always wanted more. I always believed we could go further. And I gave everything I had for this shirt.

"There were perfect afternoons and nights. There were victories I will never forget. There were defeats that still hurt to remember. I made mistakes. I suffered. There were also moments when I couldn't give the Portuguese people what they so desperately wanted. But I never gave up. And above all, I never stopped feeling proud. To represent Portugal.

"Over the years, I learned a few very simple things. Goals fade. Trophies end up in museums. Records are eventually broken. But, there is something time can never erase: the place we hold in people's hearts. If I ever made you happy, if one of my goals ever made you embrace someone, forget a worry, or feel proud of our country, then it was all worth it.

"Because being Portuguese is also about this. We suffer together, we rise together. We believe again.

"Portugal will always need young people who dare to dream. Players who never give up. New generations to believe it is possible to go where no one has ever gone before. Because a country that keeps creating new heroes is a country that never stops believing in itself.

"To my teammates, I want to say something special. Thank you for every run, for every embrace, for every argument. For every silence before stepping onto the pitch. For every victory we celebrated together. For every defeat that made us stronger. I had the privilege of being your captain, but no captain walks alone. And you will always be a part of my story.

"To all the coaches, directors, doctors, physiotherapists, kit managers, staff members, and so many others who worked alongside me throughout these years, thank you. Many of you never appeared in the photographs. But without you, none of those photographs would have been possible.

"To my family. Thank you for sharing this dream with me. Thank you for understanding the absences, the sacrifices and the moments when the national team had to take up space in my life that also belonged to you. If I came this far, it was because we always walked hand in hand.

"And to the people of Portugal. To every Portuguese person around the world, wherever you are in the world, there is one last thing I want to tell you. There is an image I will carry with me forever. The moment our national anthem begins. I look around. I see my teammates. I see the stands. I see the children, the mothers, the fathers and the grandparents. I see Portuguese people who have travelled so far just to be there. And for a few minutes, all our differences disappear. There are no clubs, there are no colours, there are no classes, there are no professions, there are no opinions. There is only one passion: Portugal.

"That is the feeling I will carry with me for the rest of my life. Today, my journey on the pitch with the national team comes to an end. I leave with my head held high, proud of the path I have taken and knowing that I gave everything I had for Portugal. But, I will never stop being one of you. I will keep suffering, cheering and celebrating every Portuguese victory with a siuuuuu!

"I spent my life working to become the best player in the world. Today, I realise my greatest victory was earning the honour of representing the best country in the world. Thank you for these 23 years. Thank you for believing in me. Thank you for allowing me to live a dream that began when I was just a little boy in Madeira running after a football. The number 7 shirt shall remain. The pride of having worn it will be mine forever. Portugal will always be a part of me. Farewell, until we meet again."

articles.title: Jesus de Miguel: Jesus Owono left out of Equatorial Guinea squad after death of Tenerife player
articles.summary: Goalkeeper Jesus Owono will miss Equatorial Guinea's Afcon 2027 qualifiers after asking to be left out of the squad following the death of Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel.
articles.body:
Goalkeeper Jesus Owono will miss Equatorial Guinea's 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) qualifiers this month following the death of Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel.

De Miguel, 30, died after suffering a serious injury in a collision with Owono during a Spanish second division match on Monday.

Owono said he is experiencing "the most difficult days of my life" in a statement issued by his club FC Andorra on Wednesday, adding that it is "very hard to come to terms with what has happened".

Equatorial Guinea's football federation (Feguifut) said that the 25-year-old had requested to be left out of coach Vincenzo Alberto Annese's squad.

Feguifut president Venancio Tomas Micha had previously said his organisation was offering "all our human and professional backing" to the player.

Owono has been first-choice keeper for the National Thunder since November 2020 and has featured at the past three Afcons.

Equatorial Guinea face Zimbabwe in a double-header in Group E, with a home match in Bata on Thursday, 12 November before a trip to Harare four days later.

The two teams sit level on three points after two rounds of matches, with DR Congo top of the standings on six points and Sierra Leone pointless at the bottom of the table.

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo: Top iconic moments from his career
articles.summary: BBC Sport looks at some of the most iconic moments from the career of Cristiano Ronaldo as he retires from international football.
articles.body:
Cristiano Ronaldo says his international career with Portugal is over, meaning the 41-year-old will just play on with Al-Nassr.

The main thing driving him on now is hoping to reach an unprecedented 1,000 career goals - he is currently on 985.

BBC Sport looks at some of the most iconic moments of a career that has also taken in spells at Sporting, Manchester United, Real Madrid and Juventus.

Ronaldo spurred on by 1,000 goals and Portugal glory

Ronaldo will not retire until he scores 1,000 goals

Untouchable or a support act? Ronaldo's 1,000-goal quest continues

After 31 first-team games and five goals for Sporting, Ronaldo caught the eye of Manchester United in a pre-season friendly in 2003, setting up two goals in a 3-1 win in Lisbon.

Ronaldo revealed that United boss Alex Ferguson took him into the dressing room afterwards to meet the players.

Five days later he joined the Red Devils for £12m.

"After we played Sporting the lads in the dressing room talked about him constantly, and on the plane back from the game they urged me to sign him - that's how highly they rated him," said Ferguson.

"He is one of the most exciting young players I've ever seen."

Ronaldo wins first Premier League title (2007)

Ronaldo won the FA Cup in his first season at United, scoring in the final against Millwall.

But it was in 2006-07 that his career really exploded. He hit 17 Premier League goals, his first season of double figures, was named player of the year and young player of the year - and won his first league title.

The following season was even better, winning his first Champions League - scoring in the final - his first European Golden Shoe for top scorer, and another league title.

Porto screamer wins Ronaldo the Puskas award (2009)

Ronaldo scored 118 goals in 292 games in his first spell at United, and one was ranked above all the others.

He hit an absolute rocket of a shot into the top corner from 40 yards in his homeland against Porto, a goal which took them into the Champions League semi-finals.

It won the inaugural Fifa Puskas award for goal of the year.

Months later, Ronaldo joined Real Madrid for £80m.

Ronaldo's Clasico winner seals Copa del Rey (2011)

Ronaldo's first season at Real Madrid produced no trophies and his second saw just the Copa del Rey won.

That final was especially notable because it is the first time Ronaldo had scored the winning goal in a final. And it was in El Clasico, one of four meetings in 18 days in all competitions.

He rose at the far post to power in a trademark header from Angel di Maria's cross in extra time as Real beat Barcelona 1-0.

Ronaldo becomes Real's top scorer (2015)

Ronaldo, then 30, scored in a 3-0 La Liga win over Levante in October 2015 to become the club's all-time top scorer with his 324th goal in 310 games.

The 2015-16 campaign would go on to be the sixth season in a row that Ronaldo scored 50 or more goals in all competitions.

Ronaldo ended up extending that record by 126 goals - leaving Real with 450 goals in just 438 games.

Euro 2016 win completes Ronaldo set (2016)

The one thing missing from Ronaldo's CV was international success.

And that came in 2016 when Portugal won the European Championship by beating hosts France 1-0 in the final in Paris.

Ronaldo ended up taking on an unofficial coaching role in that final after going off injured in tears midway through the first half.

He was named in the team of the tournament after three goals and three assists. Ronaldo retires as the top scorer in Euros history, with 14 goals.

Tearful Ronaldo becomes true great Published 11 July 2016

Ronaldo wins record fifth Ballon d'Or (2017)

Cristiano Ronaldo won his fifth Ballon d'Or, equalling Lionel Messi's record at the time, after winning the Champions League and La Liga in 2016-17. He netted twice in that European final over Juventus.

It followed on from the best player in the world awards in 2008, 2013, 2014 and 2016.

Sadly for Ronaldo, Messi would go on to win three more Ballons d'Or, meaning he won their personal rivalry 8-5.

Real legend hits 100th Champions League goal (2017)

Ronaldo became the first player to score 100 Champions League goals with a hat-trick in the 2016-17 quarter-final second leg win over Bayern Munich.

Only Messi and Robert Lewandowski have joined him to date in the century club.

Ronaldo would go on to score 141 goals in 187 games (also a record) in Europe's top competition. For six seasons in a row he was the tournament's top scorer or joint top scorer.

Bicycle kick to remember against Juventus (2018)

In 2018 came one of the most iconic moments of Ronaldo's career, maybe the greatest Champions League goal ever scored.

In the quarter-final, Ronaldo leapt into the air before acrobatically firing into the corner of the net with an incredible bicycle kick against Juventus.

Even the Juve fans stood up to applaud the player who would join their club months later.

It was nominated for the Puskas Award but he finished second to Mohamed Salah's goal for Liverpool against Everton.

The night Juventus rose to applaud Ronaldo

First player to win five Champions Leagues (2018)

Ronaldo won two La Liga titles and two Copa del Rey trophies at Real Madrid, but it was in Europe's elite club competition where he became a true legend.

He had already won the Champions League in 2008 with United, and went on to win it four more times with Real.

The first was in 2014 before a remarkable three times in a row in 2016, 2017 and 2018 (beating Liverpool in the Gareth Bale/Loris Karius final) to become the first player to win the Champions League five times.

Since his departure, former Real team-mates Toni Kroos, Dani Carvajal, Luka Modric and Nacho have gone on to win six.

Ronaldo breaks men's international goals record (2021)

Ali Daei scored 109 goals for Iran between 1993 and 2006 - and it was felt like maybe his world record for international goals in men's football would never be broken.

But Ronaldo's two late headers in a World Cup qualifying win over the Republic of Ireland in 2021 took him onto 111 goals.

He kept adding to that total and finished on 146 goals in 234 caps - also a record for international appearances.

And the last big landmark (?) as he reaches 900 goals (2024)

Ronaldo continued to smash the goals in for Juventus, in his second spell at United and at Al-Nassr but failed to really replicate many truly magic moments of the past.

However he did create some history in 2024 as he became the first player to score 900 top-level career goals as Portugal beat Croatia.

That number is now 985 - so he is only 15 off an unprecedented 1,000th goal.

He has now hit five for Sporting, 450 for Real Madrid, 145 for Manchester United, 101 for Juventus, 138 for Al-Nassr and 146 for Portugal.

He recently confirmed that he is aiming to hit the 1,000 mark.

But old rival Messi is on 931 goals, the second highest scorer ever, so Ronaldo cannot afford to dawdle too much...

articles.standfirst: El que fuera portero de Francia en el Mundial 82 disputó toda su carrera en el Mónaco
articles.summary: El que fuera portero de Francia en el Mundial 82 disputó toda su carrera en el Mónaco
articles.body: El premio One Club Man 2026, galardón con el que el Athletic reconoce a futbolistas de talla internacional que completaron toda su carrera en un mismo club, recaerá en Jean Luc Ettori (71 años) que completó su vida profesional en el Mónaco. El que fuera portero de Francia en el Mundial 1982, que les bleus jugaron como locales en San Mamés, es el segundo guardameta en tener la consideración rojiblanca tras el internacional alemán Sepp Maier (Bayern). Ettori colgó las botas en 1994 después de jugar 755 partidos en el Mónaco. Tres décadas después de su retirada continúa siendo el segundo jugador que más partidos (602) acumula en la Liga Francesa. "Me llena de orgullo recibir este premio y más aún que sea de un club con la identidad del Athletic. Es un honor recibirlo de manos de una leyenda como Iribar y formar parte de una lista de grandes nombres del fútbol mundial", ha destacado el exguardameta. El One Club Man es un premio creado en 2015 por la directiva que presidia Josu Urrutia para reconocer trayectorias de futbolistas que eligieron hacer vida deportiva en un solo club. El primer galardonado fue • Matthew Le Tissier (Southampton FC) y hasta el recién nombrado Ettori la lista la componen Paolo Maldini (AC Milan), Sepp Maier (Bayern Múnich), Carles Puyol (FC Barcelona), Billy McNeill (Celtic FC), Ryan Giggs (Manchester United), Ricardo Bochini (Independiente), João Pinto (FC Porto), Giuseppe Bergomi (Inter de Milán) y Jamie Carragher (Liverpool FC).

articles.title: Wael Mohya, la gran novedad en la lista de Alemania de Jurgen Klopp
articles.standfirst: El seleccionador alemán vuelve a mirar al futuro y premia el crecimiento del joven centrocampista, una de las caras nuevas más llamativas de la convocatoria para la Nations League
articles.summary: El seleccionador alemán vuelve a mirar al futuro y premia el crecimiento del joven centrocampista, una de las caras nuevas más llamativas de la convocatoria para la Nations League
articles.body: La segunda lista de Jürgen Klopp al frente de Alemania deja varios nombres destacados, pero pocos tan sorprendentes como el de Wael Mohya. El centrocampista se ha convertido en una de las grandes novedades de una convocatoria que combina pesos pesados como ter Stegen, Joshua Kimmich, Jonathan Tah o Wirtz con una nueva generación de futbolistas llamados a marcar el futuro de la Mannschaft. La presencia de Mohya confirma la intención de Klopp de ampliar la base de la selección y dar oportunidades a talentos emergentes. Y es que el técnico alemán no ha ocultado su admiración por el joven futbolista. "Es uno de esos casos en los que simplemente tienes que prestar atención. No hay muchos chicos de 17 años jugando actualmente en la Bundesliga. Eso por sí solo es un logro excepcional. Pero además lo está haciendo bien, muy bien", explicó el seleccionador al justificar su llamada. Lejos de presentar la convocatoria como una simple recompensa, Klopp la enmarca dentro de una estrategia a largo plazo. "He estado en contacto con él y con su familia, y hemos hablado sobre cómo queremos abordar las cosas. Estoy realmente interesado en construir el futuro junto con estos chicos, incluyendo a Wael, sin hacer promesas ni nada por el estilo", señaló. Mohya comparte protagonismo entre los nuevos nombres con futbolistas como Tom Bischof, Said El Mala, Derry Scherhant o Finn Jeltsch, símbolos de la renovación que vive la selección alemana. Klopp, de hecho, dejó claro que la convocatoria constituye también una oportunidad de aprendizaje. "Acordamos traerlo, esencialmente para que pruebe las cosas. Se trata de dejar que experimente las sesiones de entrenamiento en primera persona, porque creo que eso es importante cuando tienes la oportunidad". El técnico insistió en que el futuro del joven centrocampista dependerá de su rendimiento diario. "Por supuesto, siempre dependerá de sus actuaciones en los entrenamientos. Eso es lo lógico. Pero también se trata de ver cómo se comporta un joven, tanto dentro como fuera del campo, y de tener conversaciones con él". Y esas primeras impresiones no han podido ser mejores. "He tenido tres charlas con él hasta ahora, y todas han sido excelentes, tengo que decirlo", desveló Klopp, que incluso recurrió al sentido del humor para definir la personalidad del futbolista. "Yo no era tan seguro de mí mismo como él a los 17, ¡pero tampoco era tan bueno como él a los 17!", reconoce Klopp, quien también reconoció el gran trabajo de Füllkrug no su convocatoria.

articles.standfirst: Valoran distintos aspectos para la viabilidad de su plan como sede conjunta del Mundial 2030
articles.summary: Valoran distintos aspectos para la viabilidad de su plan como sede conjunta del Mundial 2030
articles.body: una delegación de la FIFA, compuesta por 18 integrantes, examina desde ayer las características de Bilbao y San Sebastián para convertirse en sede conjunta de cara al Mundial 2030. La premisa inicial es que San Mamés y Anoeta partiesen como distintas sedes, pero las instituciones vascas optaron por aunar la candidatura. Es lo que evalúa ahora la delegación FIFA, que ya había visitado las dos ciudades y los dos campos con anterioridad. Los enviados de la FIFA estuvieron el miércoles en San Sebastián, donde Anoeta se estaba preparando para el duelo europeo de este jueves ante el Olympique de Lyon, y este jueves visitan las instalaciones del Athletic. Los análisis de los estadios es lo más sencillo para la delegación, pues hay estándares de valoración muy concretos. El comité FIFA también se acercará a las instituciones, municipales y forales, y al Gobierno Vasco, que son las que abanderaron la idea de una candidatura única. El Mundial 2030 se celebrará de manera conjunta en España, Portugal y Marruecos. Cuando se dio forma a la propuesta tanto San Mamés como Anoeta aspiraban a convertirse en sede, acogiendo cuatro partidos cada estadio, mientras que ahora quedaria en dos por cada escenario. articles.title: Soccer star Cristiano Ronaldo announces his international retirement from Portugal
articles.summary: Soccer star Cristiano Ronaldo won’t play for Portugal anymore, ending on Thursday a career that spanned six World Cups and included a European title and the men’s all-time international scoring record.
articles.body: Soccer star Cristiano Ronaldo won’t play for Portugal anymore, ending on Thursday a career that spanned six World Cups and included a European title and the men’s all-time international scoring record. His announcement marked the end of a much lauded career that began more than two decades ago before Euro 2004 and finished with him walking out on the national team after falling out with coach Jorge Jesus. “To the Portuguese people, the day has come for me to hand back the No. 7 shirt of our national team,” the 41-year-old Ronaldo said in a long video message on social media. “I never felt it belonged to me alone but for 23 years I had the privilege and the responsibility of wearing it, defending it and carrying it with me into stadiums all around the world,” he said. “Today the time has come to pass it on to the future. It was not an easy decision because some decisions are not made with the mind alone. They are also made with the heart. A journey that began in August 2003 and changed my life forever has come to an end.” Ronaldo will keep playing at club level, which he is expected to finish at the end of this season with Al-Nassr in Saudi Arabia. He is in pursuit of his 1,000th career goal and sits on 985. Of those, a record 146 goals came in 234 appearances with Portugal. Portugal plans tribute to ‘greatest of all time’ While long-time peer Lionel Messi finished his career with Argentina last month after a much anticipated farewell match, Ronaldo’s final appearance with Portugal has ended up being on Sept. 24 in a 1-0 home win over Wales in the Nations League. Jesus kept him on the bench for the following match and said he didn’t plan to start him in the next one, so Ronaldo decided to leave the team’s training camp. Jesus later said Ronaldo would be welcome back and the decision to return was up to him. The Portuguese soccer federation released a statement expressing “deep gratitude and immense admiration” for Ronaldo’s service to the country. “Cristiano Ronaldo has raised Portugal’s profile and inspired generations of young people who dream of following in his footsteps; for many of us, he is the greatest player of all time!” the federation said. It said it intends to organize a tribute to Ronaldo “in which the fans and the country can one more time applaud and celebrate a player who has given us so much.” Ronaldo helps Portugal reach new level Before Ronaldo debuted for Portugal by replacing Luís Figo in a 2003 friendly against Kazakhstan, Portugal had never won any major trophies. Then he and successive generations of talented teammates made Portugal a regular presence at major tournaments. Portugal won its first major title at Euro 2016, and the Nations League in 2019 and 2025. “Throughout my entire career with the national team, I always pushed myself beyond my limits,” Ronaldo said. “I wanted to win. I wanted to be better. I wanted to make history. “I always demanded the most of myself. I always wanted more. I always believed we could go further. And I gave everything I had for this shirt.” Portugal qualified for the World Cup only three times before Ronaldo’s time — 1966, 1986 and 2002. On his watch, Portugal qualified every single time. The same was true for the Euros, which Portugal had played only three times before Ronaldo — 1984, 1996 and 2000. After he arrived it played in the tournament every time. Portugal was runner-up in Ronaldo’s Euro debut in 2004 at home. At the World Cup, Portugal went as far as fourth place with Ronaldo, in his tournament debut in 2006. It was among the title candidates nearly every time after that, though, with a best result a quarterfinal appearance in 2022. “There were perfect afternoons and nights. There were victories I will never forget. There were defeats that still hurt to remember,” Ronaldo said. “I made mistakes. I suffered. There were also moments when I couldn’t give the Portuguese people what they so desperately wanted. But I never gave up, I never stopped feeling proud to represent Portugal.” Portugal’s best World Cup finish remains third place in 1966 with the great Eusébio in what was the team’s only World Cup participation until 1986. A career of international records Ronaldo was the first man to score in six World Cups. He reached an all-time 11 goals at this year’s World Cup, surpassing the previous Portugal record of nine from Eusébio. He has scored for Portugal in 23 consecutive calendar years, from 2004-26. He became the first player to reach 200 men’s international appearances, and his 234 appearances remain the most all-time in men’s international soccer. Ronaldo also has the most Euro appearances with 30, and the most Euro goals with 14. His first ever international goal came at the start of Euro 2004, when host Portugal was runner-up to Greece.
