articles.title: Expert CFB Locks, Predictions for Miami vs. Notre Dame and Week 10's Biggest Games
articles.summary: We cherish each and every week of the college football season, largely because we know it won't last forever. But some weeks carry more weight when the matchups line up just right. Week 10 is one of the most sensational slates of games we've seen in some time.
articles.body:
We cherish each and every week of the college football season, largely because we know it won't last forever. But some weeks carry more weight when the matchups line up just right. Week 10 is one of the most sensational slates of games we've seen in some time.

The headliner, of course, is Notre Dame-Miami. We'll get to that, but the rest of the lineup is deep, as the stakes finally feel significant.

If you love college football, Week 10 is for you. If you love picking winners, you're in the right place.

We had our third consecutive winning week, as we've finally found a rhythm. We're 19-9-1 in that stretch. We're hoping to extend that stretch this week. At the very least, we have plenty of fascinating games to work with.

Before the season began, this felt like one of the biggest moments of the season. Thankfully, 10 weeks later, that is exactly what we have.

With that said, we have drama. We had written about this game in full, and then the news that star wideout Malachi Toney would miss the game (and time after that) with an ankle injury.

That certainly changes things in a major way for Miami, although it doesn't sway our opinion. Just the line.

Miami remains unbeaten, despite a few close calls. Notre Dame, with a road loss to BYU, has just one loss. The Irish are 4-4 against the spread; Miami is 5-3 ATS.

As for the venue, it feels significant. Not only are the Hurricanes playing this game on the road, but they will also do so with temperatures hovering somewhere in the mid-40s. We're not expecting snow or frigid rain, but the first signs of football weather have arrived.

How will that impact a team from south Florida? We'll find out.

Last week, neither team looked superb. Notre Dame started slowly against Navy before pouring it on in the second half. Miami escaped its game against North Carolina with a 38-35 win.

Quarterback Darian Mensah is still available, and the Notre Dame defense is beat up. This is certainly an opportunity for him to showcase his ability, and he has plenty of it.

As for the other side of the ball, the Irish offense should find success. The Hurricanes currently have the nation's No. 122 passing defense.

The loss of Toney moves the number, and it also drastically impacts the game. While wideouts don't normally move point spreads, this is different because Toney is different. Notre Dame stays in the playoff mix.

We likely won't know exactly how badly Texas is injured until the Missouri game, but what we know is plenty.

There are injuries and concerns on offense at running back and wide receiver. The defensive backfield has taken a hit. The team's best player, pass rusher Colin Simmons, hasn't played in weeks with an ankle injury. Throw in the loss of Trevor Goosby, the team's starting left tackle, and the concerns are massive.

When fully healthy, Texas has been inconsistent. All was well last week for the Longhorns against Mississippi State, although this team was dealing with major injuries as well.

Playing Missouri on the road feels like a different challenge entirely. After spending the last few weeks on the road, the Tigers come home. The venue has treated them well of late.

In its last two games, Missouri outscored Florida and Texas A&M by a combined score of 72-23, easily covering the spread in both matchups.

Austin Simmons has been excellent at quarterback, Jamal Roberts has been sensational at running back and the defense, which currently ranks No. 23 in scoring, has held up.

As for Texas, the Longhorns will play their second true road game of the season this week, which is hard to believe. Given the inconsistencies we've seen from Arch Manning and the offense, this might not go all that well.

Football is often a game about firepower. You either have it or you don't.

Ole Miss is by no means a perfect football team. The defense isn't ranked in the top 60 in scoring. They are also outside the top 60 in turnover margin.

But in terms of firepower—the kind of play that absolutely terrifies opposing defensive coordinators—the Rebels have a lot to offer.

Georgia has more talent. The defense is better. The roster is deeper. It also has a solid quarterback in Gunner Stockton, who has led the fourth-best scoring offense in the country.

But does this offense scare you the same way Trinidad Chambliss does on every drop back? Let's just say it's different, which it is.

Georgia clobbered Florida last week. It did so by limiting the Gators to just 252 yards of offense. The Bulldogs' offense was fine, as it didn't have to be anything more than that.

This week, however, things could be different.

Georgia passed its first major road test of the year, winning at Alabama. That experience should help greatly, although it's still a tall task. At home this year, Ole Miss has beaten LSU and delivered a dominant win over Missouri. Both of those outcomes have aged well.

This would be a significant resume boost for the Rebels. An outright win seems possible. We like the points and more.

Last week was a mess. Let's not sugarcoat it.

Ohio State, playing its first game without Julian Sayin, looked like a team playing without its starting quarterback.

Freshman Luke Fahey wasn't awful. He wasn't great, either. Still, the experience of heading to USC should pay dividends moving forward. He still has Jeremiah Smith to throw to, which should help enormously.

As for Oregon, what a weird year. The Ducks deserve credit for beating Northwestern, especially considering they were down 20-6 near halftime. Quarterback Dylan Raiola played well, which was the latest development in a bizarre, up-and-down season.

For Ohio State, playing at home will help significantly. Not just for the young quarterback, but for a team in need of an emotional boost. While the Buckeyes will benefit from a weekend at home, the Ducks have struggled playing away from home this year.

Losses to Oklahoma State and Illinois are already on the resume. This setting promises to be the most daunting to date.

Ohio State is by no means perfect. The concerns at quarterback are real. Still, this feels like a weekend to get right against a team that is a shell of what we thought it might be.

We liked Syracuse last week, although we didn't expect SMU to lose that game outright.

The Mustangs' four-game winning streak came undone on the road despite an excellent game from quarterback Kevin Jennings. In three road games this year, SMU is 1-2. The one victory came against Florida State in a tight game.

The good news is that this week's game will be played at home, which is a much-needed change of scenery.

Virginia Tech, coming off a bye, beat Clemson last time out. The offense was excellent, although the timing of the week off was probably ideal.

Outside of that win against the Tigers, however, it's hard to find a performance that really stands out for Virginia Tech. The offense certainly has plenty of talent, but the pieces haven't always fit together.

Taking on a tough offense on the road—particularly one coming off a hard-fought loss—feels like a potential mismatch. So far, the bettors haven't necessarily felt that way. The point spread has moved in the Hokies' favor.

That's not changing our minds whatsoever. SMU gets back on track with a double-digit victory.

The Bruins are legit. Despite playing without their starting QB, UCLA is unbeaten. Having a superb head coach helps. But this is a really tricky road trip and an early start time for a West Coast team. Look out.

It's a weird trip for North Carolina, coming off back-to-back heartbreaks against Syracuse and then Miami. UConn has enough offense to make this game compelling. Don't be shocked if this is a one-score game late.

We're on Utah State again. We're well aware of the fact that the offense has struggled at times. That wasn't the case last week against Colorado State. It won't be the case again against a defense that hasn't exactly been stellar.

Remember a few weeks ago when UCF beat BYU and shocked the football world? A few weeks later, the Knights are just a small favorite against a three-win team. An ugly loss to Baylor a week ago, and it was ugly, certainly played a role.

South Florida has won six games, although the team has unquestionably benefited from a favorable schedule. That's certainly evident in this point spread, which seems to favor four-win ECU.

articles.title: Spanish footballer's death: Goalkeeper Jesus Owono left out of Equatorial Guinea’s AFCON squad
articles.summary: Equatorial Guinea goalkeeper Jesus Owono has been left out of the squad for this month's Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifiers following the death of
articles.body: Equatorial Guinea goalkeeper Jesus Owono has been left out of the squad for this month's Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifiers following the death of Spanish forward Jesus de Miguel, who was involved in a fatal on-field collision with the shot-stopper during a Spanish second division match.The Equatoguinean Football Federation confirmed on Thursday that the 25-year-old would miss the upcoming qualifiers against Zimbabwe as he continues to deal with the emotional aftermath of the incident.Owono and De Miguel collided during FC Andorra's match against Tenerife on Monday. The Tenerife forward was rushed to hospital and admitted to intensive care but died on Tuesday morning, leaving the Spanish football community in mourning.Owono, who has been Equatorial Guinea's first-choice goalkeeper since his teenage years, was part of the squad for the opening two qualifiers for the 2027 AFCON finals in September. He will now miss the home fixture against Zimbabwe in Bata on November 12 and the return match in Harare on November 16.'These are the most difficult days of my life': OwonoIn a statement released by FC Andorra on Wednesday, Owono spoke about the immense emotional toll of De Miguel's death, admitting that he was struggling to come to terms with what had happened."These are the most difficult days of my life," Owono said."I struggle to find the words, and I find it very hard to process what has happened. I know there will be many questions to address, and I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect."But right now, honestly, I cannot think about anything other than Jesus and the pain we are experiencing. Rest in peace, Jesus."The goalkeeper, who has made 47 international appearances for Equatorial Guinea and featured at the last three AFCON finals, also faced online abuse following the incident. He deactivated his Instagram account on Tuesday after receiving abusive comments, with some users reportedly branding him a 'murderer'.The Equatoguinean Football Federation had earlier expressed its support for the goalkeeper, saying that he was experiencing "profound sorrow and grief" following the tragedy.Teammate defends Owono amid online abuseOwono also received public backing from FC Andorra teammate Lautaro Spatz, who took to social media to defend the goalkeeper and highlight the emotional suffering he was going through."I also want to say a few words about my teammate, goalkeeper and friend, who is deeply affected by what has happened," Spatz said. "Those of us who know him know the kind of person he is, how much he is suffering at this moment, and that he would never intentionally hurt anyone.""In football, unfortunate incidents can happen, but no one could imagine that one of them might end with such tragic consequences," Spatz added, while extending his condolences to De Miguel's family and Tenerife.FC Andorra have also made psychological support available to anyone at the club struggling to cope with the forward's death.Meanwhile, the tragedy has also triggered a case of mistaken identity online. Can Vidalet goalkeeper Michel Owono said on social media that he had been subjected to racist abuse after being confused with the Equatorial Guinea international.Spanish national police have opened a routine investigation into De Miguel's death as the football community continues to mourn the Tenerife forward.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Oficial: Raphinha firma la ampliación de contrato con el Barça
articles.standfirst: El club se asegura la continuidad de su capitán en el mejor momento de su carrera
articles.summary: El club se asegura la continuidad de su capitán en el mejor momento de su carrera
articles.body: El Barça se aseguró hoy la continuidad de su capitán: Raphinha. El Barcelona informó esta jornada de la ampliación del contrato del extremo brasileño, de 29 años, hasta 2030. El exprofesional del Leeds firma la extensión de su vínculo en el mejor momento de su carrera. Raphinha, de 29 años, y el Barça mantienen unidos sus caminos. El capitán azulgrana, que llegó al Spotify Camp Nou en verano de 2022 procedente del Leeds, extiende su vínculo con la entidad catalana dos años más, por lo que ahora finaliza su contrato en junio de 2030. El internacional también ve mejoradas sus condiciones económicas y pasa a ser uno de los profesionales mejor remunerados del vestuario culé. Deco desveló en la pasada Asamblea Ordinaria, celebrada el 19 de septiembre, que había iniciado las conversaciones con el extremo brasileño para asegurarse su continuidad durante varios cursos más, y las negociaciones han sido muy ágiles y rápidas. La pronta resolución ha sido posible porque las dos partes tenían muy claro que querían mantener el vínculo que les unía. Raphinha está feliz en Barcelona y el club y Hansi Flick apuestan por el atacante. El futbolista brasileño es un hombre fijo en el esquema del técnico alemán, que este año ha colocado al exprofesional del Leeds de falso 9, donde está mostrando el mejor rendimiento de toda su trayectoria. El internacional brasileño suma ¡19! goles este curso: 15 en LaLiga y 4 en la Champions League. Los ha marcado en 13 encuentros. Atraviesa el mejor momento de su carrera. Además de por sus excelentes prestaciones ofensivas en particular y futbolísticas en general, destacando también sus sacrificios defensivos y en la presión, Flick apuesta por Raphinha por su liderazgo, solidaridad y espíritu de equipo, de ahí que el preparador lo eligiera este curso como primer capitán del vestuario azulgrana. La presencia del técnico alemán en el banquillo también ha sido determinante en la renovación del internacional, ya que incluso el atacante ha reconocido, en más de una ocasión, que si no hubiera sido por el germano él hubiera dejado el Barça hace un par de temporadas. Considera que ha cambiado su carrera, la ha convertido en exitosa, gracias a la confianza que mostró en él.

articles.summary: Legendary striker Cristiano Ronaldo announced his retirement Thursday from international play with the Portuguese National Team.
articles.body:
Legendary striker Cristiano Ronaldo announced his retirement Thursday from international play with the Portuguese National Team.

The 41-year-old Ronaldo revealed the news in a post on social media, ending a run that saw him appear in 234 matches for Portugal since 2003:

According to Reuters , Ronaldo said, "It was not an easy decision, because there are decisions that are not made only with the head. They are also made with the heart. If I ever made you happy, if one ‌of ⁠my goals ever made you hug someone, forget a worry or feel proud of our country, then it was all worth it."

Ronaldo's retirement from international competition comes on the heels of a recent spat with the Portuguese National Team and its head coach Jorge Jesus.

Per Jessica Hopkins of The Athletic, Ronaldo left Portugal's training camp early after not being used in a UEFA Nations League match against Norway in September.

Ronaldo was fined €255 and given a 30-day suspension from the national team for his actions.

Last month, Ronaldo issued a statement in which he apologized, but noted that Jesus "broke his word" to him by not playing him against Norway.

While Ronaldo said at the time that he would remain available to play for Portugal moving forward, that is no longer the case.

Ronaldo retires as one of the most-decorated international players of all time, as his 234 international matches played and 146 goals scored are both records:

While Ronaldo was never able to lead Portugal to a FIFA World Cup triumph, he did help his country win the UEFA European Championship in 2016 and the UEFA Nations League on two occasions.

Ronaldo played in his final World Cup this past summer, scoring three goals for a Portugal side that fell to Spain in the round of 16.

With nearly 1,000 career goals for club and country, Ronaldo is the most prolific goal scorer in the history of world football.

Although his retirement from the Portuguese National Team closes a major chapter in his career, Ronaldo continues to play at the club level for Al-Nassr of the Saudi Pro League.

articles.title: Luis García Plaza: "Tenemos que rentabilizar más los momentos en que somos superiores"
articles.standfirst: El entrenador del Sevilla confirmó que Fofana e Isaac no tendrán problemas para estar ante el Alavés
articles.summary: El entrenador del Sevilla confirmó que Fofana e Isaac no tendrán problemas para estar ante el Alavés
articles.body: Este jueves, Luis García Plaza atendió a los medios en la previa de la duodécima jornada de LaLiga EA Sports, en la que el Sevilla recibirá al Deportivo Alavés en el Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán. "Un equipo que va sexto no puede hablar de que está haciendo mal las cosas. En Getafe lo hicimos muy mal en la segunda parte, es lo peor que hemos hecho. Si buscamos estar al nivel de Madrid, Barça o Atlético de Madrid, entonces sí que sacamos defectos. Pero el otro día jugamos mal la segunda parte todos, fue un mal partido", reflexionó el técnico nervionense sobre la derrota en el Coliseum. Autocrítica. "Tenemos que pensar que incluso jugando al 100% nos cuesta ganar partidos. No nos creemos mejores que nadie, tampoco peores, ya lo dije, y cada victoria ha sido dando el mil por mil. El día que no estamos acertados, no damos el máximo no salen las cosas bien, perdemos, porque somos un equipo de pico y pala". Aspecto de mejora. "Siempre hay que mejorar. Lo primero que hay que hacer siempre cuando llega una derrota es ser autocrítico. Hay que buscar el por qué, sin cambiar sistema, nos superaron. También es fútbol y es la vida, no somos máquinas, pero hay que ponerle remedio y seguir con esa concentración, con esas ganas, intentando jugar en campo contrario mucho tiempo y el otro día el Getafe nos ganó en eso en la segunda parte. Ellos le sacaron más rédito a los 45 minutos que fueron superiores que nosotros, eso creo que es otro defecto, que cuando somos superiores sacamos poco rédito y lo que tenemos que mejorar. Es verdad que hemos marcado en todos los partidos, pero tenemos que rentabilizar más los momentos de partidos que somos mejores". Sensaciones antes del parón. "Si llegamos con 20 puntos, creo que es el máximo donde podíamos estar. No debemos perder nunca la perspectiva de lo que estamos haciendo, partiendo de que el otro día el equipo es la primera vez que no está como yo quiero, eso hay que reconocerlo. Había una jugada clave, que era el segundo gol, porque ahí también habíamos metido los cambios con el 1-1 para buscar otro esquema diferente y no nos dio tiempo, que después se han reconocido en el Tiempo de Revisión que no era gol. Es una temporada muy, muy buena y no nos podemos permitir hacer esos 45 minutos del otro día". Fofana e Isaac "Pueden jugar los dos, están perfectos". ¿Stassin y Ure? "El otro día jugaron 25 minutos juntos, o sea que puede ser un recurso, pero no nosfue muy bien con ellos dos en el campo. El trabajo está bien, pero necesitamos más goles de ellos, tienen que dar ese paso adelante. Isaac lleva tres, que es una cifra para él bastante buena en comparación a minutos". Ausencia de Kochorashvili. "Kocho hoy no está porque se ha ido al entierro de Jesús de Miguel. Fue compañero suyo y se va a pegar una paliza física. Se ha ido esta mañana súper pronto para poder estar, y además me pidió permiso ayer porque la personas estamos por delante de cualquier rendimiento en un equipo, y va a llegar esta noche después de un viaje de ida y vuelta. Eso lo tenemos que tener en cuenta, incluso la emoción que va a vivir allí, entonces, eso puede ser determinante para su participación de principio o no mañana". Goles en contra. "En eso estamos trabajando, en intentar recibir menos. Es verdad que de los 11 partidos hemos dejado tres porterías a cero, y en cuatro jornadas hemos dejado uno solo. Sin embargo, son números muy exagerados en los otros, creo que tenemos que ser más regulares". Reencuentro con el Alavés. "Siempre es especial jugar contra el Deportivo Alavés, es un club donde pasé los tres años más felices de mi vida como entrenador. En Mallorca también disfruté mucho, pero fue un periodo más corto. Aquí espero disfrutar también. Me empapé de su cultura y su manera de hacer las cosas. Será mucho más especial cuando vayamos a Vitoria, pero siempre es un placer ver a todos los empleados y a muchos jugadores que estaban conmigo. Es un club modélico, les tengo que desear que pierdan y si metemos gol, lo celebraré como el que más, pero les deseo todo lo mejor". Análisis del Alavés. "Normalmente parte de una estructura de 5-3-2 o 5-4-1, aunque a veces también juegan el 4-4-2 con dos delanteros con muchísimo gol, tres incluso y el cuarto, Mañas, que es un chaval que me gusta. Lucas Boyé, Mariano y Toni son delanteros de un nivel muy importante, muy físicos, que aguantan la pelota que son rematadores. Es el equipo que más centra, es un equipo muy peligroso porque tiene dos jugadores de área que son realmente buenísimos que llevan años juntos. Te presionan alto y luego ponen un bloque más bajo donde tienes que ser muy paciente y ser muy perseverante en lo que haces porque tienen un gran contraataque, tanto con Abde como con Ángel por las bandas. Al principio a lo mejor sobrepuntuaron un poco, y en esta racha creo que tenían que haber ganado algún partido más". Roja a Manu Bueno. "Está tocado porque es una equivocación muy grande, pero en el Sevilla gana o pierde todo el mundo. Te puedo poner cientos de errores de cualquier jugador y él es uno más de la plantilla y así tiene que ser. El mal partido no deja de quitarles mérito a lo que están haciendo todos los chicos desde que empezaron".

articles.title: Álex Suárez: "Es muy difícil centrarse en lo deportivo, aunque hay pique, somos como hermanos"
articles.standfirst: El defensa de Las Palmas expresa el sentir de la plantilla
articles.summary: El defensa de Las Palmas expresa el sentir de la plantilla
articles.body: Álex Suárez puso voz al sentir de la plantilla de Las Palmas tras el fallecimiento de Jesús de Miguel. El defensa compareció visiblemente afectado: "Es la primera vez que estoy nervioso en una rueda de prensa después de siete u ocho años. Hablar de fútbol hoy es complicado, porque se trata de un compañero de profesión y club hermano. La cabeza obviamente no está en el fútbol; está con ellos y con su familia. Aquí no hay colores, somos todos unos". El futbolista recordó los estrechos vínculos entre ambos clubes y quiso trasladar el cariño y la solidaridad del vestuario en estos momentos tan difíciles. "Siempre hemos estado unidos. Somos como hermanos, aunque exista el pique deportivo. Somos clubes hermanos, siempre unidos. Los partidos serán con mucha tensión, porque todos queremos ganar. Pero nos queremos mucho, nos respetamos y estamos muy unidos". Suárez también reconoció la dificultad de centrarse en el próximo compromiso: "Es muy difícil centrarse en lo deportivo. Estas son situaciones que van más allá del fútbol. Además, se mostró partidario de detener la competición: "Se debería de parar, pero es mi opinión. Esto va más allá del fútbol. El que participa en el fútbol no está pensando en el deporte. Si los que mandan dicen que juguemos, jugaremos". Un mensaje de respeto que resumió con una petición clara: "Debemos rendirle el homenaje posible a Jesús de Miguel". En el apartado deportivo, el defensa también analizó el cambio de sensaciones que ha experimentado el equipo en las últimas jornadas. Las dos victorias consecutivas han servido para liberar la presión de un vestuario que necesitaba recuperar la confianza y mirar al futuro con otra perspectiva. Suárez reconoció que el grupo había atravesado un momento complicado, pero considera que los últimos resultados han supuesto un impulso anímico importante. "Estábamos bloqueados y las dos victorias anteriores nos liberaron la mente. Nos hacía falta ver las cosas de otra manera", ha sentenciado.

articles.title: Football: Japan's Kozo Tashima to stand against Gianni Infantino for Fifa presidency
articles.summary: Japan's Kozo Tashima has announced his candidacy for Fifa's upcoming presidential election.
articles.body:
The Japan Football Association honorary president, Kozo Tashima, has announced his intention to stand against Gianni Infantino to be the next Fifa president.

Tashima, 68, is a member of the Fifa Council and a former international footballer and coach.

He said he wants to convey "integrity, soundness, and high moral standards" and "contribute to a better future for football".

Infantino has been under intense scrutiny since it emerged he had been planning to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

The Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal was abandoned at the end of July, after significant backlash from across world football.

The deadline for candidates to stand in the election is 18 November.

Whilst support for Infantino was severely impacted by the FFE scandal, he has shored up support in recent months.

Infantino told BBC Sport last month that he felt he had the backing of the "vast, vast majority" of world football as he bids for a fourth term in charge of Fifa.

His comments came after he was "fully endorsed" by the Asian Football Confederation - following a U-turn by its president Sheikh Salman.

Former Tottenham Hotspur defender Ramon Vega was the first person to put their name forward in October for next year's Fifa presidential election.

However, Tashima's emergence as a challenger - with the backing of the Japan Football Association (JFA) - will now test the strength of Infantino's supporter base.

As with all candidates, Tashima will require the backing of five Fifa member associations.

Announcing his intentions, Tashima said: "I believe it is important to clearly communicate to the world of football the integrity, soundness, and high moral standards that Japanese football has cherished and built up over the years.

"I have decided to run for Fifa presidential election in order to convey this philosophy to the world and contribute to a better future for football.

"I will take on this challenge with strong determination, making use of the experience I have cultivated so far, and contributing to the further development of world football."

Tsuneyasu Miyamoto, president of the JFA, said: "This decision is a major challenge to contribute to the further development of world football by utilising that experience and knowledge, and at the same time, we believe it will be an opportunity to show the world the ideals and attitudes that Japanese football has cherished."

articles.title: La AFE traslada el sentir de los futbolistas: "Lo más adecuado sería suspender la jornada"
articles.standfirst: El sindicato asegura que jugadores y jugadoras de todas las categorías consideran que no existen las condiciones anímicas para competir y apelan al respeto, al duelo y a la sensibilidad tras el fallecimiento de Jesús de Miguel
articles.summary: El sindicato asegura que jugadores y jugadoras de todas las categorías consideran que no existen las condiciones anímicas para competir y apelan al respeto, al duelo y a la sensibilidad tras el fallecimiento de Jesús de Miguel
articles.body: La Asociación de Futbolistas Españoles (AFE) ha emitido un comunicado en el que asegura haber consultado a jugadores y jugadoras de todas las categorías tras el fallecimiento de Jesús de Miguel y sostiene que existe una opinión unánime dentro del colectivo. Según explica la asociación, los futbolistas consideran que no deberían disputarse los partidos previstos para esta jornada al entender que "no se dan las circunstancias anímicas ni humanas para afrontar la competición con normalidad". "Los futbolistas han expresado su profundo pesar por esta pérdida y entienden que no se dan las circunstancias anímicas ni humanas para afrontar la competición con normalidad", señala la nota. AFE añade que los jugadores han trasladado a la asociación que "lo más adecuado sería suspender la jornada", apelando "al respeto, al duelo y a la sensibilidad" ante una noticia que ha generado una profunda conmoción en el mundo del fútbol. En su comunicado, el sindicato subraya además que "el fútbol tiene una oportunidad de demostrar que, por encima de las competiciones, de los intereses deportivos y económicos y de cualquier otra consideración, están las personas", antes de concluir que "hay momentos en los que la humanidad, el respeto y la solidaridad deben estar por encima de cualquier competición". Desde Navahermosa, adonde se ha desplazado una amplia expedición de la AFE, David Aganzo ha rubricado las palabras del texto: "El mayor cariño que le podemos dar es una jornada de luto. Hay tiempo de sobra para poder competir. Creo que a nivel de España deberíamos ser ejemplares", explicó el dirigente, que ha reconocido que lo intentaron con la jornada europea pero no hubo tiempo. "Todos estamos terriblemente destrozados, y ahora competir... Estamos hablando de salud mental, pero cuando llega el momento de tomar decisiones para que esto se corte, la parte comercial de la industria, funciona", confirma Aganzo. La Asociación de Futbolistas Españoles (AFE) se ha puesto en contacto con jugadores y jugadoras de todas las categorías para conocer su sentimiento tras el fallecimiento de Jesús de Miguel. De manera unánime, el colectivo ha trasladado que considera que no deben disputarse los encuentros previstos para esta jornada. Los futbolistas han expresado su profundo a pesar de esta pérdida y entienden que no se dan las circunstancias anímicas ni humanas para afrontar la competición con normalidad. Por este motivo, han trasladado a AFE su opinión de que lo más adecuado sería suspender la jornada, apelando al respeto, al duelo ya la sensibilidad ante una noticia que ha causado una profunda conmoción entre compañeros y compañeras. Una vez más, el fútbol tiene una oportunidad de demostrar que, por encima de las competiciones, de los intereses deportivos y económicos y de cualquier otra consideración, están las personas. Porque hay momentos en los que la humanidad, el respeto y la solidaridad deben estar por encima de cualquier competición.

articles.title: Estevao ready for move Chelsea minutes under Xabi Alonso after reminder of his threat against Man Utd - The Radar
articles.summary: Estevao was finally given a chance by Xabi Alonso against Man Utd so can he now fulfil his huge potential for Chelsea? The Radar column also features the stats revealing the key to Brighton's victory over Man City as they bid to continue their strong start
articles.body:
Welcome to The Radar , a Sky Sports column in which Nick Wright uses a blend of data and opinion to shed light on need-to-know Premier League stories. This week:

🔺Estevao ready for more minutes? 🔺Gross sums up Brighton's intensity 🔺A player to watch this weekend

In the period between firing past Senne Lammens and having his goal ruled out by VAR, Estevao went over to the touchline to embrace Xabi Alonso. He had been made to wait for a first Premier League start of the season. But clearly there are no hard feelings.

Estevao's peripheral role in the opening months of the campaign frustrated Chelsea supporters, who felt his return to the side against Manchester United was overdue. On the evidence of his performance, he is determined to make up for lost time.

The 19-year-old did not get his goal in the end. But it was not for a lack of trying. He had the ball in the net twice, including the emphatic, near-post finish that preceded his hug with Alonso.

Nobody had more shots or touches in the opposition box in the game. Nobody caused United more problems or earned a louder reception from the home fans at Stamford Bridge. Estevao was a constant threat and offered impressive set-piece delivery too.

"He has had the best response, to show he deserves more, that he was prepared," said Alonso in his press conference. "Very happy for him. He deserves to enjoy this game."

Alonso felt Estevao needed time to get up to speed physically following an injury-hit first season at the club. But it was notable that the manager praised his off-the-ball work against United. "He fought really hard and at the end he was tired," he added.

It was only the second time that Estevao has played more than 75 minutes in a Premier League game. Tracking data showed he hit his highest totals for high-speed runs and running distance, offering encouragement that he is getting fitter and stronger.

It remains to be seen whether Alonso will trust him in what is likely to be a more physically demanding game against Sunderland at the Stadium of Light, live on Sky Sports on Sunday. But Estevao's chemistry with Cole Palmer might tempt him.

Estevao revealed Palmer told him they were going to do "great things together" before his arrival last summer. But injuries impacted their time on the pitch. Inauspiciously, Chelsea only won one of the seven games they both started last season.

But they certainly enjoyed each other's company last weekend. Palmer has typically gravitated towards his close friend Morgan Rogers , who has played off the left-hand side this season. The pair's relationship means they have a pre-existing understanding.

But he combined more often with Estevao to his right against United, exchanging a total of 16 passes. For context, in his previous start against Spurs, Palmer only exchanged two passes with Pedro Neto, the player who occupied the same position as Estevao.

It was striking how often Chelsea attacked down Estevao's flank.

Their attacking thirds show a roughly even split between their left and right sides in the first eight games of the season. But the percentage of attacks down the right shot up from 36 per cent to 52 per cent against United. Estevao ripped into them, supported by Josh Acheampong at right-back as well as Palmer.

The rapturous reception he received at Stamford Bridge suggests Chelsea fans will be hoping see more of him in the weeks and months ahead. Estevao is of course a thrilling talent. His attacking thrust helped make up for Joao Pedro's absence against United.

His total of 12 touches in the opposition box was more than Joao Pedro, or indeed any Chelsea player, has managed in a Premier League game this season. "He was a threat, he created many chances and situations where we could score," added Alonso.

Estevao only has two goals and two assists across his 29 Premier League appearances but his threat has been consistent. His combined average of 0.55 xG and xA per 90 minutes is the second-highest among Chelsea players since the start of last term.

The underlying data suggests he is unfortunate his numbers for goals and assists are not higher. But Joao Pedro's return from injury will soon increase the competition for places in Chelsea's attack.

Neto was moved into the false nine role against United but the Portugal international has also earned praise from Alonso for his performances on the right-hand side.

Estevao may have more to do to usurp Neto, who has contributed three goals and an assist in the Premier League so far.

The Brazilian has also been a victim of the failure to qualify for Europe. Much of his best work in his first season came in the Champions League, in which he scored three goals in seven appearances. Those opportunities are not there this term.

The lighter schedule has its advantages for the manager as he attempts to implement his way of playing and re-establish Chelsea's place among Premier League's top four. But finding a way to incorporate Estevao on a more frequent basis should be a priority after a timely reminder of his considerable quality.

Brighton host Brentford in another game live on Sky Sports on Sunday having claimed a third big scalp of the season last weekend. Their 1-0 victory over Manchester City at the Etihad Stadium owed a lot to their incredible physical intensity.

Fabian Hurzeler's side bested the hosts in all the key physical metrics, according to Premier League tracking data. Their total of 522 high-speed runs was the highest by any side in a game this season, just ahead of Arsenal's 508 in their 1-0 win against Liverpool.

Their intensity was summed up by Pascal Gross, who covered a staggering a 13.4km, the highest distance by any player in a Premier League game this season. It was all the more impressive on the back of a trip to Anfield and a Carabao Cup trip to the Etihad Stadium in the space of six days beforehand.

Player Radar: Who else to keep an eye on

Nicolas Jackson faces Manchester United on Sunday having scored three times in his last two Premier League appearances and eight times in all competitions since joining Aston Villa in the summer. Michael Carrick could do with a striker like him.

Seven Premier League games are live on Sky Sports between this weekend, starting with Everton vs Coventry City on Friday at 8pm.

Nottingham Forest then host Man City at 5.30pm on Saturday.

Sunday brings five live games, with four kicking off simultaneously at 2pm: Brighton vs Brentford , Crystal Palace vs Liverpool , Ipswich Town vs Bournemouth and Sunderland vs Chelsea .

The live coverage concludes with Man Utd vs Aston Villa at 4.30pm.

Last week's column was a defence of Kai Havertz , who duly bounced back from his misses against Fleetwood Town with a winning goal for Arsenal against Liverpool.

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s eldest son earns first Portugal U17 call-up as father brings international career to an end
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo's eldest son, Cristiano Ronaldo Jr., has made his debut for Portugal's Under-17 team shortly after Ronaldo's retirement from international play. This article discusses the implications of this milestone and the future of both father and son in football.
articles.body: Cristiano Ronaldo’s eldest son is beginning to follow a path his father has spent more than two decades defining, having earned his first call-up to Portugal’s Under-17 side for November’s European Championship qualifiers. The selection comes at a significant moment for the family: Ronaldo, 41, announced his retirement from international football on November 5, ending a Portugal career that brought him 146 goals in 234 appearances, while continuing to play for Al Nassr.Cristiano Ronaldo Jr. receives first Portugal U17 call-upCristiano Ronaldo Júnior, 16, has been included in Filipe Ramos’ 23-man squad for Portugal’s Under-17 European Championship qualifying matches, marking his first selection at that level. The Al Nassr academy forward had previously represented his country at Under-15 and Under-16 level, scoring five goals in 13 appearances across those age groups.Portugal will face Andorra on November 11, Bulgaria on November 14 and Serbia on November 17, with all three matches scheduled to take place in Lisbon. The call-up represents another step in the teenager’s international development after progressing through Portugal’s youth teams.His selection also brings a familiar surname into the national set-up at a time when his father’s own international career has just ended.Ronaldo retires from Portugal duty as his son moves upRonaldo announced on November 5 that he was retiring from international football, bringing an end to a career in which he became the leading scorer in men's international football with 146 goals in 234 appearances for Portugal. He had represented the senior national team across six World Cups and won three major international titles, including Euro 2016 and two editions of the Nations League.His departure from international football does not mark the end of his playing career. Ronaldo remains active with Al Nassr, the Saudi club where his son has developed in the academy, and is still pursuing the 1,000-goal milestone in senior football.The younger Ronaldo is not yet close to the senior national team, but his first Under-17 selection gives him another opportunity to establish himself within Portugal’s international pathway.Could Cristiano Ronaldo and his son play together?The possibility of father and son sharing a football pitch has been discussed before. Ronaldo has previously expressed an interest in playing alongside his eldest son, although he has also made clear that the decision ultimately belongs to the teenager."I would like it, but it's not something that keeps me up at night," Ronaldo said in an interview with Edu Aguirre last year."It's more in his hands than in mine. The years are passing, and eventually, I'll have to leave football. Not only physically but psychologically. But whether he plays or not, I will be a proud father regardless."Reports from Saudi Arabia earlier this year suggested that Ronaldo Jr. was close to receiving an opportunity to train with Al Nassr’s senior squad. However, he remains at the academy level, and his first Portugal Under-17 call-up is the latest indication of his progress rather than an immediate route into senior football.Ronaldo has also acknowledged that his own time as a professional is approaching its end. In an interview published in August, he told Vogue: "This is probably my last year of football, and I want to leave a spectacular legacy."For now, the two careers are moving along separate paths: Ronaldo continues his club career with Al Nassr after retiring from Portugal, while his son prepares for his first Under-17 international assignment.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Mastantuono: "El Real Madrid me ha tratado increíble"
articles.standfirst: "Bellingham me encanta", ha dicho el argentino en el programa italiano de DAZN My Skills,
articles.summary: "Bellingham me encanta", ha dicho el argentino en el programa italiano de DAZN My Skills,
articles.body: El argentino Franco Mastantuono, cedido en la Fiorentina procedente del Real Madrid, aseguró que el club blanco le trató "increíble", que tanto la entidad como sus excompañeros se comportaron de forma "impresionante" con él y que el jugador merengue que más le gusta sobre el campo es Jude Bellingham. "En el Real Madrid me han tratado increíble, o sea la gente del club, mis compañeros, impresionante", dijo el futbolista en el programa italiano de DAZN My Skills, que combina el fútbol y la técnica con el mundo de los videojuegos. "Bellingham me encanta, es el jugador que más me gusta del Madrid. Aunque están Vinicius, Mbappé, Valverde, Brahim, que es buenísimo. Ahora Diomande, Espí. Tienen un equipazo", valoró el jugador, que llegó al conjunto 'viola' este verano y firmó cedido hasta final de temporada. Mastantuono, que aterrizó en Florencia como una estrella y que se convirtió en una de las piezas centrales del equipo tras su paso por el Madrid y el River Plate, subrayó que la selección argentina cuenta con "muchos jugadores de nivel". También repasó lo que supuso para él compartir vestuario con Leo Messi, quien disputó su último partido con la albiceleste el pasado 7 de octubre. "Fue increíble, estar en un papel (en referencia a la convocatoria) o en algo del fútbol con Messi es de lo máximo para mí. Es lo máximo que le puede pasar a un jugador, porque Messi rompió todos los récords", recordó, al calificar de "muy triste" su despedida. El bonaerense, criado en la ciudad de Azul, aseveró que tuvo la posibilidad de hablar con su compatriota Gabriel Batistuta, el exfutbolista leyenda de la Fiorentina, con quien conversó sobre todo lo que él consiguió con el club de la flor de lis. Sobre la Serie A, comentó que es una liga parecida a la argentina "a nivel de choque", y que le gusta "mucho". "Es muy distinta a la española. Todos los equipos tienen mucha técnica, y eso lo hace una liga con mas posesiones, no tanto 'dribling', pero es lindo también", mantuvo. Mastantuono fue protagonista de las dos únicas victorias cosechadas por la 'Fiore' hasta el momento, tras marcar gol contra el Sassuolo y un triplete contra el Venezia. Aunque su desempeño no fue suficiente para compensar el mal arranque liguero del Fiorentina, que ocupa la decimosexta posición con dos victorias, dos empates y seis derrotas. Una situación que propició un cambio en el banquillo, con el regreso de Paolo Vanoli tras la destitución de Stefano Pioli.

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo retirement: Why has Portugal legend retired from international game?
articles.summary: As Cristiano Ronaldo retires from international football, Guillem Balague looks at why and what is next for the Portugal legend.
articles.body:
Cristiano Ronaldo's old rival Leo Messi left Argentina less than a month ago with a nation applauding him.

The Portugal legend has gone another way, and it was always going to be the case.

The 41-year-old announced his international retirement after 23 years but also after a fallout with coach Jorge Jesus which was resolved with a sanction of 30 days, that had already been served, and a fine of 255 euros.

It was the punishment imposed on the Portuguese striker for leaving the team's training camp without permission. Jesus kept him on the bench for one match and said he did not plan to start him in the next, so Ronaldo went home.

His last appearance came on 24 September against Wales. He ends his international career with 146 goals in 234 games.

A message went around Portugal with a big thank you for everything, calling Ronaldo a global ambassador and an inspiration to millions. Even so, the way it ended leaves a bit of a bitter taste.

Was he going to be named in the next squad? Possibly, as Jesus said the door was open and the decision was Ronaldo's. What is clear is that he was no longer an automatic starter, and Cristiano has never handled that well.

So is this another hissy fit? Partly, yes. He reacted the way he always has when a coach questions his place. But the label hides how much he adapted over the years.

Such a pattern appears with almost every man who sat on the Portuguese bench - there were clashes, but also communion with managers and team-mates that help explain this ending.

Ronaldo's most iconic moments as he retires from international football

Listen to the latest Football Daily podcast

When a young Ronaldo first joined the squad, he arrived at camp with his baseball cap on backwards, enormous sunglasses and headphones turned up so loud they could be heard from a distance.

He would not take the cap off to eat among veterans like Luis Figo and Rui Costa. Luiz Felipe Scolari saw an extraordinary player who was immature and obsessed with showing off. He reprimanded him in public, then told him privately that if he changed his attitude, he would one day captain Portugal.

The first great disappointment came early, and it came at home. At 19, Ronaldo played in the final of Euro 2004 at the Estadio da Luz in Lisbon, in front of a country that had convinced itself the trophy was already on its way.

A single headed goal by Angelos Charisteas was enough for unfancied Greece to win it by surprise. When the final whistle went, Ronaldo could not hold back the tears, and the image of the teenager crying on his own pitch travelled everywhere.

It was a painful way to learn what a final costs, and it left him with a hunger that never really went away.

Figo owned the number 7 at the time, so Ronaldo had to have 17. Figo helped him settle but had no intention of making it easy. When he left the national team in 2006, the shirt and the team became Ronaldo's.

In September 2005, before a qualifier in Russia, Scolari and Figo went to his room to tell him his father had died. Scolari offered to send him home. Ronaldo chose to play, asked his team-mates to behave as normal, and spent time in the dressing room doing ball tricks.

That was his way to cope with the expected but still hugely hurtful passing of his alcoholic dad. He later called Scolari "father". That way the national team had become the place that held him together.

Things went sour with Carlos Queiroz. After the 2010 World Cup exit against Spain, asked to explain a poor performance, Ronaldo told journalists to ask the coach. His influence in the camp had grown so large it changed routines and habits, which explains why the coach felt undermined.

The sociologist Joao Nuno Coelho offers the best lens on how Portugal sees him. In his analysis, the national team became a representation of Portuguese identity and of the country's need to be seen internationally.

In years of economic hardship and a crisis of confidence, a team that won admiration abroad was important beyond football.

Ronaldo stood at the centre of that need and created contradictory feelings. Some Portuguese questioned his individualism and his ego, and not everyone saw themselves in his personality.

Coelho explains criticising him became more difficult as time went by. The country wanted to be proud of him and sometimes felt uneasy at the same time.

The former international Jorge Andrade told me some supporters preferred figures like Figo, Eusebio, Paulo Futre or Rui Costa. Even so, Portugal was proud to have him. And with the titles, the doubts eased.

Under Fernando Santos in 2016, he changed. He accepted playing as a centre forward next to Nani - he had never taken a coach's instructions so naturally.

After the opening draw with Iceland, he told Nani in private that he trusted Santos, and the dressing room began to see a real captain. After missing a penalty against Austria, he barely slept. Santos woke up and found him already awake.

At the training camp in Marcoussis, he took a fan's megaphone and told supporters Portugal had won nothing yet. He was enjoying the leadership role.

In the final in Paris, he left the pitch in tears, injured. He had not had the best tournament, with a muscle complaint that did not let him perform at his best.

Nani took the armband. At half-time Ronaldo pulled himself together to encourage his team-mates, and before extra time, still limping, he told Eder he would score.

But the old instinct never fully disappeared. During extra-time, Ronaldo stood in the technical area giving orders until the fourth official sent him back. Other coaches I consulted found it excessive.

His greatest strength, the need to influence every result, also made limits hard to accept.

When he debuted in 2003, Portugal was still searching for its first major title. Some players mark an era, and others change a national team for good. He belongs to the second group.

That night in July 2016 gave Portugal its first European Championship.

Three years later he scored a hat-trick against Switzerland to put them into the first Nations League final, which Portugal won. In 2025 he lifted a second Nations League at an age when most players have retired.

No one has scored more goals for a national side, and no one has pulled on the Portugal shirt more times.

Under his influence, Portugal stopped being a gifted team and became one that arrives at every tournament expecting to contend, while a whole generation of players came through a dressing room where he decided what the standard was.

Coelho's point holds here as well: a small country found a way to be noticed, and for two decades he was its face.

After 2016 the question around him changed. Fewer asked whether he was selfish, and more asked whether Portugal depended on him too much.

In the World Cup in 2018, he scored three against Spain, including a free-kick after 45 attempts in major tournaments, and the team still went out to Uruguay.

After a difficult 2026 World Cup, much was made of him still starting up front when in fact statistically that was his best period.

Under Roberto Martinez, with 28 goals in 37 games, 0.756 per match, improves the 0.624 with Santos.

The federation has announced a special tribute to honour his contribution, and that is necessary as the exit has not left fans room for a celebration they want to be part of.

Not only they grew up with him, he took them to places they had not yet been.

articles.title: Does Kane deal end Premier League career but offer England hope?
articles.summary: Harry Kane's new deal at Bayern Munich may end his Premier League career but offers fresh hope he can lead England to glory, writes Phil McNulty.
articles.body:
Harry Kane's decision to sign a new contract with Bayern Munich carries heavy significance for the Bundesliga giants, who have been celebrating his status as a Ballon d'Or winner, but also for England and the Premier League's record books.

Bayern have acted swiftly to secure the 33-year-old on a deal taking him through to 2029 after he was crowned the world's best player, ensuring England's captain and record goalscorer will spend the final peak years of a magnificent career at Allianz Arena.

Kane has written himself into Bayern legend since joining from Spurs for £86m in August 2023, scoring 102 goals in 102 Bundesliga matches, winning two league titles and three successive Golden Boot awards.

It is why Bayern could not contemplate his departure as other clubs eyed his next move - and why the announcement Kane is staying casts ripples far beyond Munich.

Does it mean Kane will never grace the Premier League again? And does it mean - far more enticingly - he has his sights set on two more major tournaments and two more chances to grasp the prize that has eluded him at international level?

Former England striker Chris Sutton told BBC Sport: "I certainly think, although you always have to factor fitness issues into all of this, that Harry is more than capable of carrying on for a few years yet, easily.

"People might say his game lacks a little bit of pace, but he's so strong in other areas. He is a world-class all-round player. His finishing isn't going to be affected in any way by his age. He can still link up play and his football brain is first class.

"I don't see his age being such a big deal. You think of pacy players over the years who rely on that part of the game then lose it as they get older. Harry is not one of those. He seems fit and at the peak of his powers with Bayern and England."

Kane's new contract expires shortly before his 36th birthday, certainly raising the prospect the player who left Spurs as the highest scorer in their history with 280 goals in 435 appearances may never grace the Premier League again.

His consummate professionalism, and apparent ability to develop into the complete player with age, means this can never be discounted.

The notion of an emotional return to Spurs at some point has often provided background noise, but now looks increasingly unlikely.

What it surely means is that Alan Shearer will remain the Premier League's highest scorer - who knows what will happen with Erling Haaland as Manchester City await punishment after being found guilty of breaching financial regulations they deny? - and out of Kane's reach.

Shearer scored 260 goals in 441 Premier League matches for Blackburn Rovers and Newcastle United. Kane scored 213 times in 320 league games for Spurs.

With Kane still 47 short of Shearer's record, it would need a spectacular late-career flourish for him to eclipse the Geordie icon's tally to write another entry into the history books, which also have him as England's highest scorer with 91 goals from a record-equalling 125 caps.

What will be of huge interest to Thomas Tuchel - the coach who took him to Bayern and now leads England - is that Kane has delivered a clear indication that Euro 2028, to be played in the UK and Ireland, is firmly in his sights.

And, when this new deal expires, Kane is also only a year away from the 2030 World Cup, to be played in Morocco, Portugal and Spain, with special centenary opening matches held in Uruguay, Argentina, and Paraguay.

This, of course, is a stretch given the inevitable rigours of age, but few who know Kane, who have watched him move to a new level at Bayern, would ever say never to such a driven personality, hiding fierce mental strength and a competitive instinct behind his humble 'anti-superstar' persona.

Sutton said: "Euro 2028 certainly shouldn't be a problem and who knows beyond that? If Harry has got players around him with pace and dynamism, as well as runners in and around him, then his football brain isn't going to change and he can still play a huge part.

"He's such a sharp, quick, thinker. He reads the game superbly, knows where his next pass is going and has shown an ability to drop deep and impact the game.

"Harry just seems to be getting better and more rounded with age. And as for age, just look at someone like Teddy Sheringham. He was playing and scoring goals for West Ham United in the Premier League in his 40s.

"Sheringham was an incredibly talented player with supreme intelligence. Harry Kane falls right into the same category.

"Ronaldo has just retired from international football with Portugal at 41, but he is a totally different player than Harry Kane. Harry is one who can drop a little bit deeper to use his incredible ability and range of passing.

"As well as that ability, it is about how Harry's football brain works as much as anything and that won't change with age."

And it is an argument, and a hope, that is even more pertinent as England still do not possess any other striker or forward who could be considered anywhere near Kane's class or potency.

"When you talk about 2028 or 2030, who are the English strikers coming through to challenge him to take him out of the team?" said Sutton. "There's no-one in his class or effectiveness, or anywhere near it."

What also plays into the argument that Kane cannot be ruled out of such long-term involvement is the manner in which he responded so superbly to what was a disappointing Euro 2024, not only as England lost in the final to Spain but because he looked a jaded shadow of his old self.

Kane looked so out of sorts there was a clamour for him to be replaced by Ollie Watkins, then at Aston Villa. He was substituted in all of England's knockout matches, including after only 61 minutes of that final loss to Spain in Berlin.

And yet, Kane still finished as the tournament's joint top scorer with three goals from seven games.

The notion of him being replaced with the stakes so high now is unthinkable, such is his peerless form and stature.

While Bayern are convinced their new investment in Kane's brilliance will be rewarded with further honours, Tuchel will hope it is motivation and inspiration to finally end the country's long wait for international glory.

articles.standfirst: David Cubillo convoca a 21 futbolistas de la generación de 2009 para el torneo que se disputa en Catar del 19 de noviembre al 13 de diciembre, con el debut ante China el día 20
articles.summary: David Cubillo convoca a 21 futbolistas de la generación de 2009 para el torneo que se disputa en Catar del 19 de noviembre al 13 de diciembre, con el debut ante China el día 20
articles.body: España ya conoce a los suyos para el asalto al único gran título que le falta. David Cubillo hizo pública este jueves la convocatoria con la que la selección afrontará el Mundial Sub-17 de la FIFA, que se disputará en Catar del 19 de noviembre al 13 de diciembre con 48 participantes. El combinado nacional lo ha ganado todo, en categorías masculinas y femeninas, salvo esta Copa del Mundo Sub-17, que se le resiste. El técnico madrileño ha citado a 21 futbolistas, a los que se sumarán otros cuatro en el grupo de apoyo durante la preparación. El equipo se concentrará el lunes 9 por la tarde en Madrid, trabajará en la Ciudad del Fútbol de Las Rozas hasta el lunes 16 y ese día viajará a Doha para instalarse en su campo base. Conviene una precisión sobre la categoría: la lista está formada en su mayoría por jugadores de la promoción de 2009, es decir, la Sub-18 española, la misma que el mes pasado se proclamó campeona del Torneo Friendship de la UEFA. La FIFA denomina el torneo Sub-17 porque computa el año natural (del 1 de enero al 31 de diciembre), mientras que la UEFA y la RFEF se rigen por la temporada futbolística (del 1 de julio al 30 de junio). En el apartado deportivo, España debutará el 20 de noviembre ante China. El segundo rival del grupo será Fiyi, el día 23, y el grupo se cerrará frente a Marruecos el 26. Se clasifican directamente para los dieciseisavos de final los dos primeros de cada grupo, además de los ocho mejores terceros.

articles.title: Why has Cristiano Ronaldo retired from international football?
articles.summary: Portugal superstar Ronaldo calls time on international career after a falling-out with head coach Jorge Jesus.
articles.body:
Cristiano Ronaldo has announced his retirement from international football, ending a record-breaking 23-year career with Portugal.

The 41-year-old’s decision, announced on Thursday, brings an end to weeks of speculation about his international career after a public falling-out with Portugal’s head coach, Jorge Jesus.

Ronaldo is one of the most famous footballers of all time and enjoys the highest social media following of all athletes. Over the past few weeks, his millions of worldwide fans have wondered whether the forward’s career had ended on a bitter note.

Here’s a look at the events that unfolded prior to Ronaldo’s announcement:

What sparked the controversy between Ronaldo and Jesus?

On September 30, Ronaldo made an abrupt departure from Portugal’s training camp ahead of the team’s UEFA Nations League fixture against Denmark, prompting a string of questions and a few answers.

Ronaldo confirmed ⁠⁠that he had left after a ⁠⁠turbulent few hours in Copenhagen, amid reports of ⁠⁠a dispute with coach Jesus.

The captain’s decision to walk out came as a shock, as he had been due to train with his teammates at the Parken Stadium.

What happened between Ronaldo and Jesus?

Ronaldo left shortly after the head coach’s news conference, where Jesus confirmed that the five-time Ballon d’Or winner would be left out of his starting lineup for the match against Denmark, marking a second consecutive Nations League game absence.

“Following the national team manager’s press conference, and after a conversation with the President of the Portuguese Football Federation, I ⁠⁠have decided to leave ⁠⁠the national team’s training camp,” Ronaldo wrote on Instagram.

Portugal’s leading scorer had already spent the entirety of the 2-1 Nations League win away to Norway on September 27 on the bench, having captained the side in the 1-0 home victory over Wales three days before.

The game in Oslo was the first time since November 2024 that Ronaldo had not featured for Portugal despite not being injured or suspended.

The coach had indicated that Ronaldo could return to the national team ⁠⁠⁠⁠if he chose ⁠⁠⁠⁠to.

“If he wants to, he’ll return to the national team. We can talk before the next call-up, but Cris is the one who’s going ‌‌‌‌to decide,” said Jesus, who also coached Ronaldo at Saudi Arabian club Al-Nassr.

“He’s the one who should decide how he wants to end his time with the national team. In my first call-up, I said, ‘I need you, I need you to be close to me, playing or not playing, I need you’. And now I’m saying ⁠⁠⁠⁠the same thing.”

Six days later, Ronaldo accused Jesus of twice breaking his word, saying a failed agreement to publicly ⁠⁠explain his omission ⁠⁠against Norway drove him out of the camp, but insisting he remained available after any punishment.

In a lengthy statement, he gave his account of the dispute.

Ronaldo said Jesus had agreed to a plan in which the forward would miss the Norway and Denmark ⁠⁠matches to manage his fitness. However, on the day of the Norway game, the coach told him he would play for 30 minutes.

“Everyone knows the rest. I warmed up from half-time onwards, watched the minutes tick by and wasn’t called on,” Ronaldo said.

“The manager had broken his word to me.”

Ronaldo said a subsequent agreement with Jesus noted that he did ⁠⁠not require Jesus to apologise to him but said the coach’s ⁠⁠public remarks bore no resemblance to their private discussion.

“It was the second time he had broken his word to me,” Ronaldo said. “I decided to leave the training camp without waiting for any further broken promises.”

While the icon did not provide a reason for his decision, he said it wasn’t an easy one to make.

“It was not an easy decision, because there are decisions that are not made only with the head. They are also made with the heart,” Ronaldo said.

“If ⁠⁠I ever made you happy, ⁠⁠if one of my goals ever made you hug someone, forget a worry or feel proud of our country, ⁠⁠then it was all worth it.”

How did Ronaldo perform at FIFA World Cup 2026?

The record-breaking forward became the first player to play and score in six consecutive World Cups with his three goals for Portugal at the 2026 edition.

Following Portugal’s round-of-16 exit, he hinted that it was his last dance at the tournament.

“I’m sad to be leaving the World Cup like this,” he said. “I gave it my all. I did my best, and I’m leaving with a clear conscience. It was my last World Cup , yes, but I’ll now have time to reflect and be with my family.”

articles.title: Jack Grealish: David Moyes says midfielder remains unavailable for Everton's match against Coventry
articles.summary: Jack Grealish remains unavailable for Everton's Premier League clash with Coventry on Friday, manager David Moyes confirms.
articles.body:
Jack Grealish remains unavailable for Everton 's Premier League clash with Coventry on Friday, manager David Moyes has confirmed.

The on-loan Manchester City midfielder, 31, missed the Toffees' two games against Newcastle in the Premier League and Carabao Cup over the past week following a "breach of club discipline".

After Monday's win at St James' Park, Moyes said Grealish still has a future at the club but did not know when he would return to the team.

Now, speaking on Thursday before his side host Coventry , Moyes said: "No, Jack is not available.

"I wouldn't give you the plan but we will be working with Jack again soon."

Moyes and Everton have remained guarded about the issue, which is understood to have arisen from an unauthorised absence from training.

The club said he remained absent on Monday because of a lack of fitness, although Moyes said he could not comment at the time.

Asked if the upcoming international break could give Everton the opportunity to resolve the issue, Moyes added: "We just need to wait and see how things go."

Grealish is trying to rebuild his career at Everton , having fallen out of favour at City despite costing the club £100m in 2021.

Grealish, who played a key role helping City win the 2022-23 Treble, will be out of contract at the end of the season.

He scored twice in 22 games for Everton last season during a loan spell which was cut short by injury.

The midfielder returned to the club for a second loan spell this season but had only made six appearances before falling out of favour.

articles.title: Orian Goren y Adeyemi, la cara y la cruz
articles.standfirst: El joven futbolista ha sido citado por Israel, mientras que el extremo no irá con Alemania
articles.summary: El joven futbolista ha sido citado por Israel, mientras que el extremo no irá con Alemania
articles.body: Orian Goren y Adeyemi representan, por el momento, la cara y la cruz de las convocatorias internacionales. Mientras que el joven centrocampista se estrenará en una cita con la selección absoluta de Israel, el extremo alemán no ha entrado en los planes de su combinado nacional para el próximo parón. El centrocampista continúa dando pasos en su progresión. Goren ya había sido convocado en la anterior ventana internacional por la selección sub-21 de Israel, a pesar de tener solo 17 años. Sin embargo, su buen momento no ha pasado desapercibido y ahora ha recibido la llamada de la absoluta. El joven futbolista está viviendo un momento dulce. Había sido incluido por Hansi Flick en las convocatorias para el Clásico y el encuentro de Champions League del pasado martes contra el Aston Villa. Israel afrontará dos compromisos durante el próximo parón internacional, en los que se medirá a Kosovo y Austria. . La otra cara de la moneda es Adeyemi. El extremo alemán, que había regresado a las convocatorias de su selección durante el anterior parón internacional, se ha quedado esta vez fuera de los planes de Jürgen Klopp. Así, ambos futbolistas afrontan el próximo parón internacional desde situaciones muy diferentes: mientras Orian Goren vive su primera gran oportunidad con la absoluta de Israel, Adeyemi tendrá que esperar una nueva ocasión para regresar a la dinámica de la selección alemana.

articles.title: Real Sociedad - O. Lyon en directo | Última hora de Europa League en vivo hoy
articles.summary: Once de la Real Sociedad Matarazzo sale de inicio con Unai Marrero; Aramburu, Zubeldia, Sarr, Sergio Gómez; Gorrotxategi, Herrera; Guedes, Oyzarzabal,
articles.body:
Muy buenas tardes. Arrancamos con la narración en directo del partido que va a enfrentar a Real Sociedad y Olympique de Lyon , correspondiente a la jornada 4 de la UEFA Europa League. Un encuentro de los más potentes que se pueden ver en esta edición de la competición entre dos equipos que aspiran a clasificarse directamente para octavos de final sin tener que pasar por por la ronda de play-off. Para ello, ambos necesitan sumar hoy los tres puntos en juego. El Lyon tiene seis puntos por cuatro de la Real y ocupan la decimotercera y la decimocuarta posición respectivamente.

La Real Sociedad viene de perder en Liga , con polémica, en el derbi vasco ante el Athletic pero, hasta ese momento, el equipo de Matarazzo había conseguido una racha de resultados bastante buena, ya que llevaba cinco partidos en los que solo había cedido un empate.

El conjunto txuriurdin tiene tres bajas confirmadas para el choque de esta tarde. Son Odriozola, Beitia y Zakharyan . Por lo demás, se espera que el técnico disponga sobre el terreno de juego su once de gala.

El Olympique de Lyon afronta este partido en una situación bastante anómala ya que su técnico , Paulo Fonseca , decidió rescindir su contrato para marcharse al Sporting de Portugal. Será Jorge Maciel, el que se haga momentáneamente cargo del equipo en el día de hoy. El cuadro francés ha viajado hasta Donosti con bajas importantes . Pierde para este partido a su goleador Nuamah, autor de seis goles, Morton, Niakhaté, Sulc y Openda.

El partido comienza a las 18.45 horas en el estadio de Anoeta. El colegiado designado para este partido es el griego Anastasio Papapetrou , mientras que en el VAR estará Angelos Evangelou . articles.title: Unai Emery: Aston Villa boss close to new contract at club
articles.summary: Aston Villa manager Unai Emery is close to agreeing a contract extension at the club.
articles.body:
Aston Villa head coach Unai Emery is close to agreeing a contract extension at the club - which will hand him even more responsibility for long-term development.

The Villa boss held talks with the hierarchy on Wednesday to discuss the club's future, with all parties keen on extending his time at Villa Park.

Emery would relish the opportunity to play an even bigger role in developing the club for the long term, with talks ongoing about the fine details, the finances, and the length of the new deal.

The plan is to announce the new contract once all details have been agreed, which is unlikely to be before the weekend.

Emery, whose team won the Europa League in May – Villa's first major trophy in 30 years – celebrated four years at the club last month.

In his time at Villa he has transformed the side, from a group who were in a relegation fight to one who have qualified for European football every season under his management.

The Spaniard has been linked with a move to Manchester United , who Villa play this weekend at Old Trafford, should they sack boss Michael Carrick.

Emery, though, who was already under contract until 2029, is now close to signing a new longer-term deal.

On Wednesday night, Villa released a statement saying a meeting had taken place between Emery, club chairman Nassef Sawiris, executives Roberto Olabe and Damian Vidagany.

The club said: "The discussions focused on jointly planning the club's long-term strategic direction, with positive discussions establishing a clear commitment beyond 2029 for the joint development of the club under the sporting leadership of Unai Emery based on the shared ambitions and common goal to reach excellency and keep growing during the next years.

"The objective is clear: to build an ambitious, competitive Aston Villa capable of taking on the biggest challenges and achievements."

Emery, a former Arsenal , Sevilla and Paris St-Germain boss, joined Villa in 2022 from Villarreal.

After a tumultuous summer in which the spine of Emery's side that finished fourth in the Premier League and lifted European silverware was sold, Villa are currently 10th in the Premier League and have won three of their four opening matches in the Champions League.

Villa threatened pundit and former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher with legal action last month after he suggested Emery would be a good choice if Manchester United were looking for a new manager, with Carragher also telling fans of the club to "shut up". However, Villa dropped the threat after he apologised.

articles.title: Top Japan FA official to stand against Infantino for FIFA presidency
articles.summary: Kozo Tashima second person to declare he will challenge Infantino, after former Spurs defender Ramon Vega.
articles.body:
Kozo Tashima, honorary president of the Japan Football Association, said on Thursday he will stand against Gianni Infantino in FIFA’s presidential election in March.

Tashima is the second person to declare he will challenge Infantino, following former Tottenham defender Ramon Vega .

The 68-year-old Tashima, who has served on the FIFA Council, said in a statement: “With the full support of the JFA I have decided to declare my candidacy in the FIFA presidential election.

“I believe it is important that the sincerity, integrity and high ethical standards that Japanese football has long valued and built up are clearly communicated to the global football community.

“In order to share these principles with the world and contribute to a better future for football, I have decided to run in the FIFA presidential election.”

Tashima, who was JFA president from 2016 to 2024, added, “Drawing on the experience I have gained over the years, I will take on this challenge with firm resolve so that I can contribute to the further development of world football.”

The deadline for candidates to declare for the election is November 18.

Incumbent Infantino, who is seeking to be re-elected to a fourth and final term as FIFA president, had faced stinging criticism and calls to quit after his aborted World Cup selloff plan.

But Infantino is now in a strong position to secure re-election after the Asian Football Confederation endorsed the 56-year-old last month.

Infantino earlier said he had the backing of the “vast, vast majority” of member associations, and dismissed calls for him to go.

articles.title: JAL vuelve a La Rosaleda sin haber perdido contra el Málaga
articles.standfirst: El asturiano vivió un desamor en la Costa del Sol
articles.summary: El asturiano vivió un desamor en la Costa del Sol
articles.body: La etapa de José Alberto López en el Málaga CF terminó de una manera muy diferente a como el técnico asturiano había imaginado. Su llegada a La Rosaleda en la temporada 2021-22 suponía, a su juicio, una oportunidad para dar un salto importante en su trayectoria y liderar un proyecto a medio plazo, con el objetivo de devolver al equipo a Primera División. Sin embargo, la situación del vestuario se deterioró rápidamente y la goleada encajada ante el Ibiza (0-5) en Martiricos precipitó su destitución. Manolo Gaspar, entonces director deportivo, optó por prescindir de sus servicios en un contexto de fuerte presión social. Años más tarde, el propio Gaspar admitiría que aquella decisión había sido un error. Desde su marcha, el entrenador asturiano no ha ocultado su malestar con la forma en la que se produjo su salida. En diferentes comparecencias públicas, publicaciones en redes sociales y, especialmente, en sus visitas a La Rosaleda al frente del Racing de Santander, ha dejado distintos mensajes hacia el que fue su antiguo equipo. Su motivación por conseguir buenos resultados en Martiricos tampoco ha pasado desapercibida. Una de sus declaraciones más significativas llegó después de conseguir el ascenso a Primera División con el conjunto cántabro. "Me he sentido, por primera vez, entrenador profesional de verdad después de las experiencias anteriores. Me han dado la posibilidad de desarrollar un proyecto que se ve culminado con este ascenso", afirmó entonces, en unas palabras que muchos interpretaron como una comparación con su anterior etapa en Málaga. En 2024, antes de regresar a la Costa del Sol, volvió a referirse abiertamente a su destitución. "Lo que ha pasado después de mi destitución, todos lo saben. Yo allí he sido feliz, creo que se fue muy injusto conmigo, terriblemente injusto. Forma parte del fútbol, no seré el primero ni el último entrenador al que echen. Para tomar esas decisiones se tienen que analizar muchas más cosas que un resultado", explicó. Hay, no obstante, un detalle de aquella salida que merece ser recordado. José Alberto renunció al 20% de la cantidad que tenía pendiente de cobrar de su contrato, una cifra que rondaba los 250.000 euros. Un gesto que supuso un importante alivio económico para el Málaga en una etapa especialmente complicada para las arcas de la entidad. También existe una particular estadística que alimenta la historia entre el técnico y el conjunto blanquiazul. Desde que abandonó el banquillo malaguista, el Málaga no ha conseguido derrotar a ningún equipo dirigido por José Alberto. Ambos se han enfrentado en cinco ocasiones, con un balance de tres victorias para el asturiano y dos empates. Además, el entrenador tampoco perdió frente a los malagueños en sus enfrentamientos anteriores a su llegada a La Rosaleda.
